objects.description: Function returning a string literal that describes a Janus API error code. No custom struct/enum/typedef types are defined in this header; only integer macros for error codes and this function declaration exist. Pointer type shown is the pointer form of the function’s return type, as no user-defined types are present.
Enumeration of configuration element kinds used throughout the config API: any (for searches), plain item, category, and array.

Generic node in a configuration tree. It may represent a plain item (name/value), a category (name with a list of children), or an array (name with an ordered list of children). The list field is used only for category/array; value is used only for item.

Root configuration object representing a parsed or programmatically built configuration. Holds a name, a flag indicating libconfig (.jcfg) versus INI, and the top-level list of containers (items/categories/arrays).

Although declared as a variable, it is a constant array defining the available prefixes used by the logging macros in this header.

Alias type for the Janus mutex abstraction. It maps to pthread_mutex_t when USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX is defined, otherwise to GMutex. Used with the janus_mutex_* macros for init, lock, trylock, unlock, and destroy. Underlying lifetime and semantics follow the backing implementation (pthread or GLib).

Alias type for the Janus condition variable abstraction. It maps to pthread_cond_t when USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX is defined, otherwise to GCond. Use with janus_condition_* macros for init, wait, timed wait/until, signal, broadcast, and destroy. Semantics and lifetime follow the backing implementation.
Enumeration of media kinds supported by the recorder: audio, video, or data. Used to tag/handle the type of media being recorded.

Opaque recorder object holding state and metadata to persist RTP packets into a Janus .mjr file. Manages file path/name, codec info, RTP extensions, timestamps, media type, optional Opus RED PT, encryption flag, write/pause state, RTP switching context, locking, destroyed flag, and reference counting. External fields like GHashTable, gint64, gboolean, janus_rtp_switching_context, janus_mutex, gint, and janus_refcount are defined elsewhere.
Enumeration of RTCP packet types as defined by RFC3550 and related specs. Used to identify the RTCP packet kind.
RTCP common header with version, padding, reception report count/FC field, packet type, and length. Bitfield layout depends on endianness.
Sender Information section of an RTCP Sender Report containing NTP/RTP timestamps and sender packet/octet counts.
RTCP report block with per-source reception statistics (fraction lost, cumulative lost, highest seq, jitter, last SR, delay).
RTCP Sender Report packet including common header, sender SSRC, sender info and at least one report block (array may extend).
RTCP Receiver Report packet including common header, receiver SSRC and at least one report block (array may extend).
RTCP SDES chunk header identifying the SSRC the SDES items refer to.
An SDES item within an RTCP SDES chunk, with type, length and variable-length content (array is extensible).
RTCP SDES packet composed of a header and at least one chunk and item (variable-length, may be followed by padding).
direct_api_constructors: int janus_rtcp_sdes_cname(char *packet, int len, const char *cname, int cnamelen)

objects.description: RTCP BYE packet signaling end of participation; contains one or more SSRCs (array extensible).
RTCP APP packet for application-defined use; includes a 4-char name and possible app-dependent payload following.
NACK FCI entry (per RFC4585) containing the lost packet ID and bitmask of additional lost packets.
Internal Janus linked-list node holding an RTP sequence number to be retransmitted.
REMB FCI structure used in PSFB AFB messages, carrying bitrate estimation and up to three SSRCs.
direct_api_constructors: int janus_rtcp_remb(char *packet, int len, uint32_t bitrate)
int janus_rtcp_remb_ssrcs(char *packet, int len, uint32_t bitrate, uint8_t numssrc)
int janus_rtcp_cap_remb(char *packet, int len, uint32_t bitrate)

objects.description: FIR FCI structure requesting an intra-frame; contains target SSRC and sequence number (upper 24 bits reserved).
Generic RTCP Feedback message (RTPFB/PSFB). Contains header, sender and media SSRC, and variable-length FCI area.
RTCP XR report block header plus variable-length content. Block type and type-specific fields define semantics.
RTCP Extended Reports packet containing the sender SSRC and one or more XR blocks.
Internal Janus RTCP state used to compute/track stats (seq cycles, jitter, RTT, loss, link quality, etc.) across RTP/RTCP processing.
Container for transport-wide congestion control feedback: RTP transport sequence number and its receive timestamp.

RTP header struct per RFC 3550. Contains version/flags/CSRC count, payload type and marker, sequence number, timestamp, SSRC, and a zero-length CSRC array placeholder. Used to parse and update RTP headers.
Container for an RTP packet buffer and metadata such as length, creation time, retransmission timing/backoff, and parsed plugin RTP extensions. The lifetime/ownership of data is not specified here.
Represents the 16-bit ID (type) and 16-bit length of an RTP header extension block (one-byte/two-byte header family context dependent).
Layout for RFC 2833/4733 telephone-event RTP payload: event code, end flag, reserved bit, volume level, and duration.

objects.description: Enumeration of supported audio codecs. Utility functions exist (declared here) to map names and payload types, but constructors are not applicable.
Enumeration of supported video codecs.
State used to rewrite RTP headers coherently across SSRC changes and to compensate for skew. Tracks last/prev sequence and timestamp, offsets, delays, and timing references.
Tracks AV1 SVC state gleaned from Dependency Descriptor RTP extensions: template count/offset, a map of templates, available spatial/temporal layers, and whether state changed.
Represents a simplified AV1 Dependency Descriptor template with template ID and associated spatial/temporal layers.

Holds state to process simulcast RTP streams: RID extension ID, per-substream AV1 SVC contexts, current/target substream and temporal layer, drop policy, last relay time, and flags indicating changes/PLI needs.

Tracks SVC forwarding decisions (VP9/AV1): desired and target spatial/temporal layers, drop trigger, per-layer last-received times, and change/PLI flags; embeds an AV1 DD context for when DD data is present.

Enumeration of SRTP crypto profiles supported by this header abstraction. Values map to common SRTP cipher/auth suites, including AES-128 CM with SHA1 (32- and 80-bit auth tags) and AEAD AES-GCM (128- and 256-bit). Used to select the SRTP protection profile when configuring sessions.

Internal Janus SDP session-level object. Holds global SDP fields, lists of attributes and media lines, plus lifetime/ownership (destroyed flag and refcount). Used as the root container when parsing, manipulating, and serializing SDP.
Enumeration of SDP m-line media types (audio, video, application, or other).
Enumeration for media direction attributes for m-lines (sendrecv, sendonly, recvonly, inactive); DEFAULT maps to sendrecv. INVALID is used during parsing for errors.
Representation of a single SDP m-line, including media type, port/proto, payload formats, connection info, bandwidth, direction, and per-m-line attributes, with refcounting/teardown support.
Container for an SDP a= attribute (name/value) with optional direction hint (e.g., for extmap). Managed object with refcount and destroyed flag.

objects.description: Enumeration of name-value directive tokens used to drive automatic SDP offer/answer generation APIs (offer, offer m-line, and answer). Values control which media to include, directions, mids/msids, codecs, payload types, extensions, profiles, etc.
Enumeration of bitmask flags controlling how network interfaces are matched: by name, IPv4, IPv6, any IP, or any. Values are designed to be OR-combinable.
Configuration object describing a device lookup query. It can match by interface name and/or IP address (IPv4/IPv6), governed by the mode flags. Contains parsed IPv4/IPv6 values when applicable.
Tagged union holding either an IPv4 or IPv6 address. The family field must be AF_INET or AF_INET6 to indicate which union member is valid.
Tagged buffer for human-readable string representations of IPv4/IPv6 addresses. The family indicates which buffer (ipv4 or ipv6) contains the string.
Describes a single expected JSON parameter: its name, expected JSON type, and validation flags. Used by validation macros to check JSON objects.

objects.definition: typedef gsize janus_flags;
objects.description: Alias for a bitset container used to store Janus flags. Underlying type is gsize; manipulated via janus_flags_* helpers.
Tracks VP8 simulcast sequencing (picture IDs and temporal indices) to keep continuity across SSRC/source switches.
Holds SVC-related fields parsed from a VP9 payload descriptor: spatial/temporal layers and descriptor flags.
Represents a single RED (RFC 2198) block: payload type, timestamp offset, data pointer and length.

Intrusive reference counter to embed as a member inside other objects. Holds an atomic integer counter and a destructor callback to be invoked when the count drops to zero. Intended for manual memory management without garbage collection; users initialize it to 1 and adjust via provided macros. The free callback must locate and free the owning object (typically with janus_refcount_containerof).

Opaque-ish recorder object managing dumping of RTP/RTCP/data packets either as text (for later text2pcap conversion) or directly to legacy pcap. Holds target filename, FILE handle, truncation limit, output mode, writability flag, and an internal mutex. Create with janus_text2pcap_create, use janus_text2pcap_dump to append packets, then close/free via janus_text2pcap_close and janus_text2pcap_free. The file may be appended if an existing filename is reused. Thread-safety is coordinated via the embedded janus_mutex.
Enumeration of packet types that the recorder can dump: RTP packets, RTCP packets, or generic data packets. Utility function janus_text2pcap_packet_string converts a value to a string.

Interface of function callbacks the Janus core exposes to plugins, used by plugins to push events, relay RTP/RTCP/DataChannel data, request keyframes/REMB, manage PeerConnections and sessions, emit events, and validate auth tokens.

The plugin interface a dynamic plugin must implement to integrate with Janus core: lifecycle, metadata, session management, message handling, media/data callbacks, and session queries. typedef create_p is the factory function signature returning janus_plugin*.
Opaque mapping object representing a session/handle between a plugin and the Janus core. Holds opaque core and plugin pointers, a stopped flag, and a reference counter.

Return value container for janus_plugin::handle_message (and admin messages) indicating result type (OK, OK_WAIT, ERROR), optional explanatory text, and optional JSON content. Ownership rules are documented in comments; content is unref'd by destroy.
RTP packet wrapper exchanged between core and plugins, including stream index, media type, payload buffer and length, plus parsed/desired RTP extensions.

Container for supported RTP header extensions parsed from or to be applied to an RTP packet (audio level/VAD, video orientation, playout delay, dependency descriptor, absolute capture time, and scalability layers).
RTCP packet wrapper exchanged between core and plugins, including stream index, media type, and payload buffer and length. May carry compound RTCP.
SCTP DataChannel message wrapper containing channel label, optional subprotocol, binary/text flag, payload buffer and length.
Enumeration describing the outcome of a plugin request: error, immediate success with response, or accepted with asynchronous follow-ups.

/* Use forward declaration to avoid including jansson.h */
typedef struct json_t json_t;
objects.description: Forward-declared opaque Jansson JSON value type used throughout the API for messages, JSEP, and responses. Definition is external; only pointer usage is valid here.

Callback interface implemented by the Janus core and provided to transport plugins. Transports use these functions to submit incoming requests, report transport disconnects, validate API secrets/tokens when needed, and publish events to event handlers.

Interface a transport plugin must implement. The struct holds function pointers for lifecycle, metadata, capability checks, messaging to clients, session lifecycle notifications, and a management/query hook.
Mapping object between Janus core and a transport-side session/connection. Holds an opaque transport pointer, optional deleter, a destroyed flag, a mutex, and a reference counter.

objects.definition: typedef janus_transport* create_t(void);
objects.description: Function type for the factory hook exported by a transport plugin. The function returns a pointer to the plugin’s janus_transport instance. The core dlsyms a symbol typically named create matching this type.

Typedef alias forward-declared earlier; full definition provided in this header as struct janus_transport_callbacks. Pointer type repeated here to satisfy alias mapping. Note: This entry is deduplicated above; see main janus_transport_callbacks object.

Typedef alias forward-declared earlier; full definition provided in this header as struct janus_transport. Pointer type repeated here to satisfy alias mapping. Note: This entry is deduplicated above; see main janus_transport object.

Typedef alias forward-declared earlier; full definition provided in this header as struct janus_transport_session. Pointer type repeated here to satisfy alias mapping. Note: This entry is deduplicated above; see main janus_transport_session object.

Event handler plugin interface object for Janus. Implementations fill this struct with function pointers that the core calls to initialize, destroy, query metadata, receive events, and synchronously handle admin requests. The events_mask field (janus_flags) indicates which event types the handler subscribes to. Implementers must ensure json_t reference management (json_decref when done) for incoming_event data. Details about janus_flags come from utils.h and are not defined here.

objects.definition: typedef janus_eventhandler* create_e(void);
objects.description: Function type for the plugin factory symbol that event handler shared objects must export. The function takes no parameters and returns a pointer to a statically or dynamically allocated janus_eventhandler instance.

Main logger plugin interface object for Janus. It is a function table (vtable-like struct) that a logger module populates to integrate with the Janus core. The core calls these callbacks to initialize/destroy the plugin, query metadata, deliver log lines, and handle admin requests. The struct itself holds only function pointers; the plugin typically exposes a single static instance. All callbacks are mandatory per documentation; missing ones will cause rejection by the core.

objects.definition: typedef struct janus_logger janus_logger;
objects.description: Typedef alias that names the logger interface struct type. Use janus_logger as the canonical type name for the function-pointer table defined later in this header.

objects.definition: typedef janus_logger* create_l(void);
objects.description: Function type for the logger factory symbol a plugin must export to be loaded by the Janus core. A function of this type, typically named create (per documentation string mentions create_l hook), returns a pointer to the plugin's janus_logger instance. Note: this is a function pointer type, not a data object type.

functions.name: janus_get_api_error
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string corresponding to a Janus API error code. Intended for logging, debugging, or user-facing error messages when handling results from the Janus web-based JSON API. If the provided code matches one of the JANUS_ERROR_* (or JANUS_OK) constants in this header, the function returns a descriptive string for that code. Behavior for unknown codes is not documented; it likely returns a generic string, but this is unspecified.
requirements: error should be a valid Janus API error code (e.g., JANUS_OK or one of the JANUS_ERROR_* values defined in this header); passing arbitrary integers may yield an unspecified/"unknown" description.
The returned pointer is a const char*; the caller must not modify or free the returned string (assumed to be a static or internally managed string).

Thread-safety and lifetime of the returned pointer are not documented; callers should treat the returned string as read-only and assume it remains valid at least until the next call, but no guarantees are documented.

functions.name: janus_config_parse
functions.description: Parses an INI (or supported configuration) file into a janus_config structure. Use when loading configuration from disk; returns NULL on failure.
requirements: config_file must point to a readable file path
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect parse/load failures
On success, the returned janus_config must be released with janus_config_destroy

functions.name: janus_config_create
functions.description: Creates a new empty configuration with the provided name.
requirements: name should be a valid, non-NULL string identifying the configuration (inferred from parameter purpose)
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation/creation failure
On success, the returned janus_config must be released with janus_config_destroy

functions.name: janus_config_print
functions.description: Prints the configuration to standard output using logging level LOG_VERB. Use for debugging/inspection.
requirements: config must refer to a valid, initialized janus_config instance
This prints at LOG_VERB; use janus_config_print_as to choose a different level

functions.name: janus_config_print_as
functions.description: Prints the configuration to standard output using the specified logging level. Use when a level other than LOG_VERB is desired.
requirements: config must refer to a valid, initialized janus_config instance
level must be a valid debugging/logging level for the application (exact accepted values are unspecified)

functions.name: janus_config_save
functions.signature: int janus_config_save(janus_config *config, const char *folder, const char *filename);
functions.description: Saves a configuration to a file at folder/filename. Returns 0 on success, negative on failure.
requirements: config must refer to a valid, initialized janus_config instance
folder must be a valid, writable directory path (inferred from purpose)
filename should include the desired extension; recommended .jcfg (or .cfg for legacy INI files)
Caller must check the integer return value: 0 indicates success; negative indicates failure

functions.name: janus_config_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a janus_config instance and all associated resources.
requirements: config must be a janus_config previously obtained from janus_config_parse or janus_config_create
After destruction, the config pointer must not be used again (use-after-free hazard)

functions.name: janus_config_item_create
functions.description: Creates a new configuration item with the given name and optional value.
requirements: name must be a valid, non-NULL string
value is optional and may be NULL (as documented)
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation/creation failure
The returned item should be added to a configuration container via janus_config_add or equivalent

functions.name: janus_config_category_create
functions.description: Creates a new configuration category container with the specified name.
requirements: name must be a valid, non-NULL string
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation/creation failure
The returned category should be added to a configuration via janus_config_add

functions.name: janus_config_array_create
functions.description: Creates a new configuration array container with the specified name.
requirements: name must be a valid, non-NULL string
Caller must check for NULL return to detect allocation/creation failure
The returned array should be added to a configuration via janus_config_add

functions.name: janus_config_container_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a configuration container (item, category, or array). If the container is a category or array, destroys all contained elements too. Does not unlink from its parent.
requirements: container must be a valid janus_config_container (item/category/array)
If the container is currently linked to a parent, the caller must unlink it from the parent before or after calling this function; this function will not unlink it automatically (per note)
After destruction, the container pointer must not be used again

functions.name: janus_config_get
functions.signature: janus_config_container *janus_config_get(janus_config *config, janus_config_container *parent, janus_config_type type, const char *name);
functions.description: Looks up an item, category, or array by name and type within a parent container or at the root when parent is NULL. Returns NULL if not found or if a type mismatch occurs.
requirements: config must be a valid janus_config instance
If parent is non-NULL, it must be a category or array within the same configuration (inferred from parameter description)
type specifies the expected container type; if the found element's type does not match, NULL is returned (documented)
If parent is NULL, lookup is performed at the root (documented)
name should be a valid, non-NULL string for the element to search

functions.name: janus_config_get_create
functions.signature: janus_config_container *janus_config_get_create(janus_config *config, janus_config_container *parent, janus_config_type type, const char *name);
functions.description: Same as janus_config_get, but creates the element if it does not exist. If type is janus_config_type_any, no creation is performed.
requirements: config must be a valid janus_config instance
If parent is non-NULL, it must be a category or array within the configuration (inferred)
type determines the kind of element to find or create; if type is janus_config_type_any, nothing is created (documented)
name should be a valid, non-NULL string
Caller must check for NULL return to detect failure to find/create

functions.name: janus_config_search
functions.description: Variadic helper to look up an item, category, or array. Returns a matching container or NULL if not found or type-mismatched. Exact varargs contract is not documented here; likely represents a path specification.
requirements: config must be a valid janus_config instance
Varargs usage/termination is unspecified in this header; callers must consult implementation or higher-level docs to supply correct arguments (unknown details)
If a matching element is found but with mismatched type, NULL is returned (documented)
Caller must check for NULL return

functions.name: janus_config_add
functions.description: Adds an item/category/array to a category or array in the configuration. In categories, an existing element with the same name is replaced; in arrays, the element is appended and duplicates are allowed. Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: config must be a valid janus_config instance
If parent is provided, it must be a category or array (documented)
item must be a valid janus_config_container (item/category/array) to add
Caller must check the integer return value: 0 indicates success; negative indicates failure
Replacing occurs when adding to a category and an element with the same name already exists; arrays accept duplicates and append (documented)

functions.name: janus_config_remove
functions.description: Removes an existing item/category/array with the specified name from a category or array (or from the root when parent is NULL). Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: config must be a valid janus_config instance
parent should be the category/array to remove the element from, or NULL for root (documented)
name must be a valid, non-NULL string naming the element to remove
Caller must check the integer return value: 0 indicates success; negative indicates failure

functions.name: janus_config_get_items
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated GList of plain items either at the root or under the specified parent container.
requirements: config must be a valid janus_config instance
If parent is non-NULL, it must be a category or array (documented)
The returned GList is newly allocated; the caller must free the list itself
The list data (the contained pointers) must NOT be freed by the caller because they are linked from the configuration (documented)
Caller must check for NULL return on failure

functions.name: janus_config_get_categories
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated GList of categories either at the root or under the specified parent container.
requirements: config must be a valid janus_config instance
If parent is non-NULL, it must be a category or array (documented)
The returned GList is newly allocated; the caller must free the list itself
The list data (the contained pointers) must NOT be freed by the caller because they are linked from the configuration (documented)
Caller must check for NULL return on failure

functions.name: janus_config_get_arrays
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated GList of arrays either at the root or under the specified parent container.
requirements: config must be a valid janus_config instance
If parent is non-NULL, it must be a category or array (documented)
The returned GList is newly allocated; the caller must free the list itself
The list data (the contained pointers) must NOT be freed by the caller because they are linked from the configuration (documented)
Caller must check for NULL return on failure

functions.name: janus_vprintf
functions.description: Buffered, printf-style logging function that enqueues formatted output for asynchronous I/O (e.g., stdout, files, external loggers). Output may not appear immediately due to buffering. Use like printf with a GLib-compatible format string and matching variadic arguments.
requirements: janus_log_init must be successfully called before using this function.
format must be a valid GLib/printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format string types.
Do not rely on immediate output; logging is buffered and may be delayed.

functions.name: janus_log_init
functions.signature: int janus_log_init(gboolean daemon, gboolean console, const char *logfile, GHashTable *loggers);
functions.description: Initializes the buffered logger, creating the buffer pool and the processing thread. Configure whether Janus runs as a daemon, whether to print to stdout, an optional logfile path, and optional external loggers via a GHashTable.
requirements: Must be called before any other logging functions (including janus_vprintf).
Return value must be checked: 0 indicates success; a negative integer indicates failure.
logfile may be NULL if no file-based logging is desired (inferred from "if any").
loggers may be NULL if no external loggers are registered (inferred from "if any").

functions.name: janus_log_reload
functions.description: Reopens the current log file to support log rotation. Intended to refresh the file handle used for file-based logging without restarting the process.
requirements: Should be called only after successful janus_log_init (inferred).
Has effect only if file-based logging is enabled and a logfile is configured (inferred).

functions.name: janus_log_destroy
functions.description: Shuts down the buffered logger, tearing down the processing thread and buffer pool and releasing resources.
requirements: Call only after janus_log_init has succeeded (inferred).
Should be called once during shutdown to avoid resource leaks (inferred).
Do not call other logging functions after destruction (inferred).

functions.name: janus_log_is_stdout_enabled
functions.description: Returns whether stdout logging is currently enabled.
requirements: Meaningful only after janus_log_init has been called (inferred).

functions.name: janus_log_is_logfile_enabled
functions.description: Returns whether file-based logging is currently enabled.
requirements: Meaningful only after janus_log_init has been called (inferred).

functions.name: janus_log_get_logfile_path
functions.description: Returns the full path to the configured log file, or NULL if none. Ownership/constness of the returned pointer is not documented here and is therefore unknown; consult the implementation or higher-level docs before freeing or modifying.
requirements: May return NULL if no logfile is configured.
Caller should not assume ownership or mutability of the returned string based solely on this declaration (unknown; not specified).
Meaningful only after janus_log_init has been called (inferred).

functions.name: janus_mutex_init
functions.description: Initializes a Janus mutex wrapper (backed by pthread_mutex_t). Usage: pass a valid pointer to an uninitialized janus_mutex; the macro calls pthread_mutex_init(a, NULL).
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for a janus_mutex
a must not already be initialized
Only valid when compiled with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_mutex_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a Janus mutex (pthread back end). Frees any resources associated with the mutex.
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex
The mutex must not be locked by any thread when destroying (pthread requirement)
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_mutex_lock_nodebug
functions.description: Locks a Janus mutex without debug logging (pthread back end). Wraps pthread_mutex_lock(a). Blocks until the mutex is acquired.
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex
Caller must not already hold a non-recursive mutex to avoid deadlock (matches pthread semantics)
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_mutex_lock_debug
functions.description: Locks a Janus mutex with debug logging (pthread back end). Prints the file/function/line and the mutex address before calling pthread_mutex_lock(a).
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_mutex_lock
functions.description: Locks a Janus mutex, optionally with debug logging depending on the global lock_debug flag (pthread back end).
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex
If lock_debug is non-zero, logging is emitted prior to locking
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_mutex_trylock_nodebug
functions.signature: void janus_mutex_trylock_nodebug(janus_mutex *a)  // macro: assigns to a variable named 'ret' in the caller's scope
functions.description: Attempts to acquire the mutex a without blocking, with no debug logging. This is a macro wrapper over the platform try-lock primitive (pthread_mutex_trylock or g_mutex_trylock). It does not return a value; instead it assigns the try-lock result to a caller-provided variable named ret. Under USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX, ret is set to 1 on success and 0 on failure; under the GLib backend, ret is set to a gboolean (TRUE on success, FALSE on failure). Use when you want a non-blocking lock attempt without emitting debug output.
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex (initialized via janus_mutex_init or static initializer).
This macro requires a variable named ret to be declared and visible in the caller’s scope before invocation.
When compiled with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX, ret must be an int-compatible type receiving the value !pthread_mutex_trylock(a) (1 on success, 0 otherwise).
When compiled without USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX (GLib), ret must be of type gboolean (or compatible) receiving the value g_mutex_trylock(a).
The mutex a must be unlocked for the try-lock to succeed; otherwise ret will indicate failure.
Do not assume the macro yields an expression; it cannot be used in places where a value is required (e.g., in a conditional directly).
Callers must handle the case where the try-lock fails (ret indicates failure) without using the mutex-protected resource.
The mutex must eventually be released with janus_mutex_unlock(a) if ret indicates success.

functions.name: janus_mutex_trylock_debug
functions.signature: void janus_mutex_trylock_debug(janus_mutex *a)  // macro: assigns to a variable named 'ret' in the caller's scope and logs a debug line
functions.description: Attempts to acquire the mutex a without blocking, emitting a debug log line indicating the file, function, line, and mutex address. This macro wraps the platform try-lock primitive and, like the nodebug variant, assigns the result to a caller-provided variable named ret instead of returning a value. Under USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX, ret is set to 1 on success and 0 on failure; under the GLib backend, ret is set to a gboolean (TRUE on success, FALSE on failure).
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex (initialized via janus_mutex_init or static initializer).
This macro requires a variable named ret to be declared and visible in the caller’s scope before invocation.
When compiled with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX, ret must be an int-compatible type receiving the value !pthread_mutex_trylock(a) (1 on success, 0 otherwise).
When compiled without USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX (GLib), ret must be of type gboolean (or compatible) receiving the value g_mutex_trylock(a).
The macro logs via JANUS_PRINT and should only be used when such logging is acceptable.
The mutex a must be unlocked for the try-lock to succeed; otherwise ret will indicate failure.
Do not assume the macro yields an expression; it cannot be used in places where a value is required (e.g., in a conditional directly).
Callers must handle the case where the try-lock fails (ret indicates failure) without using the mutex-protected resource.
The mutex must eventually be released with janus_mutex_unlock(a) if ret indicates success.

functions.name: janus_mutex_trylock
functions.description: Attempts to lock a Janus mutex (pthread back end). Returns non-zero on success (lock acquired) and zero on failure (already locked). Uses selective debug logging controlled by lock_debug.
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex
Safe to call even if the mutex is already locked by another thread; will not block and returns 0 in that case
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_mutex_unlock_nodebug
functions.description: Unlocks a Janus mutex without debug logging (pthread back end). Wraps pthread_mutex_unlock(a).
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex
The calling thread must currently hold the mutex
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_mutex_unlock_debug
functions.description: Unlocks a Janus mutex with debug logging (pthread back end). Logs the file/function/line and mutex address before calling pthread_mutex_unlock(a).
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex
The calling thread must currently hold the mutex
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_mutex_unlock
functions.description: Unlocks a Janus mutex, optionally logging depending on lock_debug (pthread back end).
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex
The calling thread must currently hold the mutex
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_condition_init
functions.description: Initializes a Janus condition variable (pthread back end). Wraps pthread_cond_init(a, NULL).
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for a janus_condition
a must not already be initialized
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_condition_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a Janus condition variable (pthread back end). Wraps pthread_cond_destroy(a).
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_condition
No threads may be waiting on or using the condition variable when destroying
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_condition_wait
functions.description: Waits on a condition variable (pthread back end). Atomically releases the mutex and waits until signaled or broadcast, then re-acquires the mutex. Wraps pthread_cond_wait(cond, mutex).
requirements: cond must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_condition
mutex must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex
The calling thread must hold mutex when calling wait (standard pthread requirement)
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_condition_wait_until
functions.signature: int janus_condition_wait_until(janus_condition *cond, janus_mutex *mutex, long long end_time_us)  // pthread backend
functions.description: Timed wait on a condition variable (pthread back end). Converts an absolute microsecond timestamp to struct timespec and calls pthread_cond_timedwait(cond, mutex, &ts). Note: the macro discards the return value; use is for side effects only.
requirements: cond must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_condition
mutex must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_mutex and must be locked by the caller
end_time_us is expected to be an absolute time in microseconds (typically from a monotonic clock, e.g., g_get_monotonic_time()); exact clock base is not guaranteed by this header
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_condition_signal
functions.description: Signals one waiter on a condition variable (pthread back end). Wraps pthread_cond_signal(cond).
requirements: cond must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_condition
A suitable mutex should protect the associated predicate before/after signaling (standard practice)
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_condition_broadcast
functions.description: Wakes all waiters on a condition variable (pthread back end). Wraps pthread_cond_broadcast(cond).
requirements: cond must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized janus_condition
A suitable mutex should protect the associated predicate before/after broadcasting
Only valid with USE_PTHREAD_MUTEX defined

functions.name: janus_recorder_init
functions.description: Initialize the recorder subsystem. Optionally configures recorder files to be created with a temporary extension while writing, which can then be renamed on close. Typical usage: call once at process/plugin startup before creating any janus_recorder instances.
requirements: Must be called before creating or using any janus_recorder instances.
If tempnames is TRUE, extension should point to a valid, non-empty file extension string to append during recording (inferred from parameter docs).
The function performs global initialization; calling it multiple times without matching deinit may lead to undefined behavior (inferred from typical init/deinit patterns).
No return value; failures, if any, are not reported via this API.

functions.name: janus_recorder_deinit
functions.description: De-initialize the recorder subsystem and release any global resources acquired by janus_recorder_init.
requirements: Should be called once when recorder functionality is no longer needed, after all janus_recorder instances have been closed/destroyed (inferred from typical init/deinit patterns).
Must not be called concurrently with janus_recorder_init or while other threads are creating/using recorders (inferred).

functions.name: janus_recorder_create
functions.signature: janus_recorder *janus_recorder_create(const char *dir, const char *codec, const char *filename);
functions.description: Create a new recorder instance that writes RTP packets for a single medium to a Janus .mjr file. If dir is NULL, the current directory is used; if filename is NULL, a random filename is chosen. The function may attempt to create dir if it does not exist.
requirements: dir may be NULL to default to the current working directory; otherwise it should be a valid, writable filesystem path.
codec must name a supported codec ("vp8", "opus", "h264", "g711", "vp9").
filename may be NULL to auto-generate; otherwise it should be a valid filename (no path separators if combined with dir).
On success returns a non-NULL janus_recorder*; caller must check for NULL and handle failure.
The returned recorder must eventually be closed (janus_recorder_close) and destroyed (janus_recorder_destroy) to avoid resource leaks (inferred).

functions.name: janus_recorder_create_full
functions.signature: janus_recorder *janus_recorder_create_full(const char *dir, const char *codec, const char *fmtp, const char *filename);
functions.description: Create a new recorder with additional codec-specific details. Behaves like janus_recorder_create but allows passing fmtp (e.g., H.264 or VP9 profile) for inclusion in the recording header.
requirements: dir may be NULL to default to the current working directory; otherwise it should be a valid, writable path.
codec must name a supported codec ("vp8", "opus", "h264", "g711", "vp9").
fmtp may be NULL if no codec-specific parameters are needed; otherwise it should be a codec-appropriate parameter string.
filename may be NULL to auto-generate; otherwise it should be a valid filename.
On success returns non-NULL; caller must check for NULL and handle failure.
The recorder must be closed and destroyed when no longer needed (inferred).

functions.name: janus_recorder_pause
functions.description: Pause recording on a recorder instance so subsequent frames are not written until resumed. Intended for temporary suspension of output without destroying the recorder.
requirements: recorder must be a valid, initialized janus_recorder pointer.
Return value is 0 on success and a negative integer on error; caller must check and handle non-zero results.
While paused, calling janus_recorder_save_frame will not write frames (behavior implied by "pause"/"resume").

functions.name: janus_recorder_resume
functions.description: Resume recording on a previously paused recorder instance so that subsequent frames are written again.
requirements: recorder must be a valid, initialized janus_recorder pointer.
Return value is 0 on success and a negative integer on error; caller must check and handle non-zero results.
Should be called after janus_recorder_pause to re-enable writing (inferred).

functions.name: janus_recorder_add_extmap
functions.signature: int janus_recorder_add_extmap(janus_recorder *recorder, int id, const char *extmap);
functions.description: Add an RTP header extension mapping to the recording metadata so it is reflected in the .mjr header. This is only allowed before the first frame is written.
requirements: recorder must be a valid, initialized janus_recorder pointer.
Must be called before the first frame is written; calling it after that will return an error (explicit).
id is the numeric RTP extension ID; must correspond to the intended RTP header extension for this stream (numeric requirement explicit; specific range not documented).
extmap must be a valid, non-NULL namespace URI/token describing the RTP extension.
Returns 0 on success, negative integer on error; caller must check and handle non-zero results.

functions.name: janus_recorder_description
functions.description: Set a human-readable description string for this recording, to be stored in the recording metadata/header.
requirements: recorder must be a valid, initialized janus_recorder pointer.
description should be a valid, null-terminated string; behavior for NULL is unspecified in the header.
Returns 0 on success, negative integer on error; caller must check and handle non-zero results.

functions.name: janus_recorder_opusred
functions.description: Mark this recording as using Opus RED (redundant encoding) and record the RED payload type in the header. Only allowed before the first frame is written.
requirements: recorder must be a valid, initialized janus_recorder pointer.
Must be called before the first frame is written; calling it after that will return an error (explicit).
red_pt is the payload type value used for RED in this stream (exact valid range not documented here).
Returns 0 on success, negative integer on error; caller must check and handle non-zero results.

functions.name: janus_recorder_encrypted
functions.description: Mark this recording as containing end-to-end encrypted media (e.g., via Insertable Streams) so the .mjr header reflects this. Encrypted recordings will not be processable by janus-pp-rec without decryption.
requirements: recorder must be a valid, initialized janus_recorder pointer.
Must be called before the first frame is written; calling it after that will return an error (explicit).
Returns 0 on success, negative integer on error; caller must check and handle non-zero results.
Callers should be aware that post-processing with janus-pp-rec will not work out of the box for encrypted recordings (explicit note).

functions.name: janus_recorder_save_frame
functions.description: Append a single RTP frame to the recorder file. The buffer should contain the raw RTP packet data to store in the .mjr file for later post-processing.
requirements: recorder must be a valid, initialized janus_recorder pointer that is currently writable and not paused (inferred from fields and pause/resume API).
buffer must point to a readable memory region containing the frame to save; it should represent a complete RTP packet.
length must be the size in bytes of buffer; it should be greater than 0 and match the actual buffer size (inferred).
Returns 0 on success, negative integer on error; caller must check and handle non-zero results.

functions.name: janus_recorder_close
functions.description: Close the recorder, flushing and closing the underlying file. After closing, the recorder should no longer be used to save frames.
requirements: recorder must be a valid, initialized janus_recorder pointer.
Should be called once per recorder when recording is finished, before destroying the recorder (inferred).
Returns 0 on success, negative integer on error; caller must check and handle non-zero results.
After a successful close, do not call janus_recorder_save_frame on this recorder (inferred).

functions.name: janus_recorder_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a recorder instance and free its resources. Intended to be called after closing to release memory and handles.
requirements: recorder may be NULL (behavior not specified; typically safe to no-op in many APIs, but not guaranteed—unspecified).
Should not be used after destruction; any further access is invalid (inferred).
If the recorder is still open, caller should close it before destroying to avoid data loss (inferred).

functions.name: janus_rtcp_context_get_rtt
functions.description: Returns the estimated round-trip time (RTT) stored in the given RTCP context. Intended for querying the current RTT estimate after RTCP processing has updated the context.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid, initialized janus_rtcp_context structure.
The context should have been updated by RTCP processing to provide a meaningful RTT value.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_context_get_lost_all
functions.description: Returns the total number of lost packets, either remote-reported or locally computed, from the RTCP context.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid, initialized janus_rtcp_context structure.
remote selects which metric to read: TRUE for peer-reported loss, FALSE for locally computed loss.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_context_get_jitter
functions.description: Returns the interarrival jitter from the RTCP context, either the peer-reported (remote) or locally computed value.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid, initialized janus_rtcp_context structure.
remote selects which metric to read: TRUE for peer-reported jitter, FALSE for locally computed jitter.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_context_get_in_link_quality
functions.description: Returns the inbound link quality estimation stored in the RTCP context.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid, initialized janus_rtcp_context structure.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_context_get_in_media_link_quality
functions.description: Returns the inbound media link quality estimation stored in the RTCP context.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid, initialized janus_rtcp_context structure.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_context_get_out_link_quality
functions.description: Returns the outbound link quality estimation stored in the RTCP context.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid, initialized janus_rtcp_context structure.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_context_get_out_media_link_quality
functions.description: Returns the outbound media link quality estimation stored in the RTCP context.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid, initialized janus_rtcp_context structure.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_swap_report_blocks
functions.signature: void janus_rtcp_swap_report_blocks(char *packet, int len, uint32_t rtx_ssrc);
functions.description: Reorders Report Blocks inside an RTCP RR/SR so that the media SSRC’s block comes first when an RTX SSRC appears first. Useful to normalize blocks before further processing.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing an RTCP packet (RR/SR with report blocks).
len must be the size in bytes of the packet buffer.
rtx_ssrc must be the RTX SSRC to compare against.
The buffer must be large enough to contain the RTCP header and at least two report blocks if a swap is expected.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_get_sender_ssrc
functions.description: Extracts and returns the sender SSRC from an RTCP packet, for quick demultiplexing (e.g., BUNDLE). Returns 0 on error.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing an RTCP packet.
len must be the size in bytes of the packet buffer.
The RTCP must contain a sender SSRC field in its first report (e.g., SR/RR/FB).

functions.name: janus_rtcp_get_receiver_ssrc
functions.description: Extracts and returns the receiver/media SSRC from an RTCP packet for demultiplexing. Returns 0 on error.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing an RTCP packet.
len must be the size in bytes of the packet buffer.
The RTCP must contain a receiver/media SSRC field in its first report block or feedback message.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_check_len
functions.description: Validates that an RTCP packet is at least the minimum size (8 bytes) and that the RTCP length field matches the actual buffer size.
requirements: rtcp must point to the start of an RTCP packet header within the buffer.
len must be the total number of bytes available for this RTCP packet (>= 8).

functions.name: janus_rtcp_check_rr
functions.description: Checks whether the buffer could contain a valid RTCP Receiver Report (RR). Returns TRUE if the packet is consistent with an RR.
requirements: rtcp must point to the start of an RTCP packet header within the buffer.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP packet.
The function expects the RTCP header type to be RR and lengths to be consistent.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_check_sr
functions.description: Checks whether the buffer could contain a valid RTCP Sender Report (SR). Returns TRUE if the packet is consistent with an SR.
requirements: rtcp must point to the start of an RTCP packet header within the buffer.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP packet.
The function expects the RTCP header type to be SR and lengths to be consistent.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_check_fci
functions.signature: gboolean janus_rtcp_check_fci(janus_rtcp_header *rtcp, int len, int sizeof_fci);
functions.description: Checks whether the buffer could contain a valid RTCP Feedback Message (RTPFB/PSFB) with a defined, fixed-size FCI entry. Returns TRUE if sizes and counts are consistent.
requirements: rtcp must point to the start of an RTCP packet header within the buffer.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP packet.
sizeof_fci must be the size in bytes of a single FCI entry for the feedback type being validated and should be a positive integer.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_check_remb
functions.description: Checks whether the buffer could contain a valid AFB REMB RTCP message. Returns TRUE if a REMB is plausibly present and sizes are consistent.
requirements: rtcp must point to the start of an RTCP packet header within the buffer.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP packet.

functions.name: janus_is_rtcp
functions.description: Quickly inspects a buffer to determine if it contains RTCP (as opposed to other protocols). Returns TRUE if it looks like RTCP.
requirements: buf must point to at least the minimum RTCP header size (>= 8 bytes).
len must be the size of the buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_parse
functions.description: Parses and validates an RTCP message. Optionally updates the provided RTCP context. Returns 0 on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing one or more RTCP packets (compound allowed).
len must be the size in bytes of the RTCP data.
ctx may be NULL if no context updates are needed; otherwise it must point to a valid janus_rtcp_context.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_fix_report_data
functions.signature: int janus_rtcp_fix_report_data(char *packet, int len, uint32_t base_ts, uint32_t base_ts_prev, uint32_t ssrc_peer, uint32_t ssrc_local, uint32_t ssrc_expected, gboolean video);
functions.description: Adjusts fields in incoming RTCP SR/RR report data (e.g., timestamps/SSRCs) to align with local stream context. Returns the number of fields updated, negative on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing an RTCP SR or RR (or compound containing them).
len must be the size in bytes of the RTCP data.
base_ts and base_ts_prev must be RTP context base timestamps used to compute offsets.
ssrc_peer is the remote SSRC for this stream; ssrc_local is the local SSRC; ssrc_expected is the SSRC expected in this RTCP.
video indicates whether the report refers to video (affects timestamp scaling).

functions.name: janus_rtcp_fix_ssrc
functions.signature: int janus_rtcp_fix_ssrc(janus_rtcp_context *ctx, char *packet, int len, int fixssrc, uint32_t newssrcl, uint32_t newssrcr);
functions.description: Parses an RTCP message and, if requested, rewrites sender/receiver SSRCs according to draft-ietf-straw-b2bua-rtcp. Returns 0 on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing one or more RTCP packets.
len must be the size in bytes of the RTCP data.
fixssrc controls behavior: non-zero to modify SSRCs, zero to only parse.
newssrcl is the sender SSRC to set; newssrcr is the receiver SSRC to set when fixssrc is enabled.
ctx may be NULL if context updates are not needed; otherwise must be valid.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_filter
functions.description: Filters an outgoing RTCP compound packet, possibly removing messages per policy (per b2bua-rtcp draft). Returns a pointer to the filtered data, or NULL if all messages were removed. Sets newlen to the size of the filtered packet.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing one or more RTCP packets.
len must be the size in bytes of the RTCP data.
newlen must be a valid pointer to receive the length of the filtered result.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_process_incoming_rtp
functions.signature: int janus_rtcp_process_incoming_rtp(janus_rtcp_context *ctx, char *packet, int len, gboolean rfc4588_pkt, gboolean rfc4588_enabled, gboolean retransmissions_disabled, GHashTable *clock_rates);
functions.description: Processes the header of an incoming RTP packet to update the associated RTCP context (sequence tracking, jitter, loss, etc.). Supports RTX (RFC4588) and retransmission settings. Returns 0 on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid janus_rtcp_context (optional only if no updates are required; typically non-NULL).
packet must point to a buffer containing a single RTP packet.
len must be the RTP packet length in bytes (must cover at least the RTP header).
rfc4588_pkt should be TRUE if this packet is an RTX packet.
rfc4588_enabled should be TRUE if the stream uses RTX.
retransmissions_disabled should be TRUE if retransmissions are not supported for this stream.
clock_rates is an optional mapping (GHashTable) from payload types to clock rates; may be NULL.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_report_block
functions.description: Fills a report_block structure using statistics from the RTCP context for inclusion in a Receiver Report. Returns 0 on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: ctx must point to a valid, initialized janus_rtcp_context with up-to-date statistics.
rb must point to writable memory for a janus_report_block within an RTCP packet being built.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_has_bye
functions.description: Checks whether an RTCP message (possibly compound) contains a BYE packet. Returns TRUE if found.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing RTCP data.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP data.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_has_fir
functions.description: Checks whether an RTCP message (possibly compound) contains a FIR (Full Intra Request). Returns TRUE if found.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing RTCP data.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP data.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_has_pli
functions.description: Checks whether an RTCP message (possibly compound) contains a PLI (Picture Loss Indication). Returns TRUE if found.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing RTCP data.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP data.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_get_nacks
functions.description: Parses an RTCP NACK feedback message and appends the requested sequence numbers to the provided queue for retransmission.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing RTCP data with at least one NACK feedback message.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP data.
nacks_queue must be a valid, initialized GQueue that will receive sequence numbers to retransmit.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_remove_nacks
functions.description: Removes an RTCP NACK message from a compound RTCP packet after handling its sequence numbers. Returns the new length of the message. Current behavior removes the whole NACK rather than individual entries.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing an RTCP message that includes a NACK.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP data.
Caller should handle the returned new length and resulting modified buffer content.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_get_remb
functions.description: Inspects a compound RTCP packet for a REMB (Receiver Estimated Max Bitrate) and returns the reported bitrate. Returns 0 if no REMB is available.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing RTCP data.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP data.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_cap_remb
functions.signature: int janus_rtcp_cap_remb(char *packet, int len, uint32_t bitrate);
functions.description: Modifies an existing REMB inside an RTCP packet to cap the reported bitrate at a specified value. Returns 0 on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a buffer containing RTCP data with an existing REMB message.
len must be the length in bytes of the RTCP data.
bitrate is the new bitrate to report (e.g., 128000).

functions.name: janus_rtcp_sdes_cname
functions.signature: int janus_rtcp_sdes_cname(char *packet, int len, const char *cname, int cnamelen);
functions.description: Generates a new RTCP SDES packet containing a CNAME item. Returns the message length in bytes on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a writable buffer for the RTCP SDES message.
len is the size of the buffer in bytes (must be sufficient for the SDES header, chunk, and CNAME item).
cname must point to the CNAME string data; cnamelen is its length in bytes.
The CNAME item must fit within the provided buffer.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_remb
functions.signature: int janus_rtcp_remb(char *packet, int len, uint32_t bitrate);
functions.description: Generates a new RTCP REMB feedback message reporting the specified bitrate. Returns the message length in bytes on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a writable buffer of at least 24 bytes.
len must be exactly 24 per the documentation comment (MUST be 24).
bitrate is the bitrate to report (e.g., 128000).

functions.name: janus_rtcp_remb_ssrcs
functions.signature: int janus_rtcp_remb_ssrcs(char *packet, int len, uint32_t bitrate, uint8_t numssrc);
functions.description: Generates a new RTCP REMB feedback message for multiple SSRCs reporting the specified bitrate. Returns the message length in bytes on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a writable buffer of at least 24 bytes.
len must be exactly 24 per the documentation comment (MUST be 24).
bitrate is the bitrate to report (e.g., 128000).
numssrc is the number of SSRCs to include in the REMB.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_fir
functions.description: Generates a new RTCP FIR (Full Intra Request) to ask for a keyframe. Increments the provided FIR sequence number. Returns the message length in bytes on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a writable buffer of at least 20 bytes.
len must be exactly 20 per the documentation comment (MUST be 20).
seqnr must be a valid pointer; it will be incremented by the function.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_fir_legacy
functions.description: Generates a legacy RTCP FIR (RFC2032) message to request a keyframe. Same as janus_rtcp_fir but with packet type 192. Returns the message length in bytes on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a writable buffer of at least 20 bytes.
len must be exactly 20 per the documentation comment (MUST be 20).
seqnr must be a valid pointer; it will be incremented by the function.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_pli
functions.description: Generates a new RTCP PLI (Picture Loss Indication) request for a keyframe. Returns the message length in bytes on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a writable buffer of at least 12 bytes.
len must be exactly 12 per the documentation comment (MUST be 12).

functions.name: janus_rtcp_nacks
functions.description: Generates a new RTCP NACK message listing lost RTP packets for retransmission. Returns the message length in bytes on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a writable buffer of at least 16 bytes.
len must be exactly 16 per the documentation comment (MUST be 16).
nacks must be a GSList of packet identifiers to NACK.

functions.name: janus_rtcp_transport_wide_cc_feedback
functions.signature: int janus_rtcp_transport_wide_cc_feedback(char *packet, size_t len, guint32 ssrc, guint32 media, guint8 feedback_packet_count, GQueue *transport_wide_cc_stats);
functions.description: Generates a Transport-Wide Congestion Control (TWCC) RTCP feedback message containing reception statistics. Returns the message length in bytes on success, -1 on errors.
requirements: packet must point to a writable buffer (at least 16 bytes per the comment, and large enough for the full TWCC content).
len is the size of the provided buffer in bytes and must be sufficient for the generated message.
ssrc is the sender SSRC of the feedback; media is the media SSRC being reported.
feedback_packet_count is the TWCC feedback packet count field.
transport_wide_cc_stats must be a GQueue of janus_rtcp_transport_wide_cc_stats entries describing received packets.

functions.name: janus_rtp_extension_id
functions.description: Returns the numeric ID associated with a known RTP header extension namespace string. Intended to map a known extmap URI to its internal/known identifier. Details of the mapping are not documented here.
requirements: type should point to a NUL-terminated string naming an RTP header extension namespace (e.g., one of the JANUS_RTP_EXTMAP_* constants).

functions.name: janus_audiocodec_name
functions.description: Returns a string name for the provided audio codec enum value.
requirements: acodec should be a valid janus_audiocodec enumerator.

functions.name: janus_audiocodec_from_name
functions.description: Parses an audio codec name and returns the corresponding janus_audiocodec enumerator.
requirements: name should point to a NUL-terminated codec name string.

functions.name: janus_audiocodec_pt
functions.description: Returns the (default) RTP payload type number for the specified audio codec, if any.
requirements: acodec should be a valid janus_audiocodec enumerator.

functions.name: janus_videocodec_name
functions.description: Returns a string name for the provided video codec enum value.
requirements: vcodec should be a valid janus_videocodec enumerator.

functions.name: janus_videocodec_from_name
functions.description: Parses a video codec name and returns the corresponding janus_videocodec enumerator.
requirements: name should point to a NUL-terminated codec name string.

functions.name: janus_videocodec_pt
functions.description: Returns the (default) RTP payload type number for the specified video codec, if any.
requirements: vcodec should be a valid janus_videocodec enumerator.

functions.name: janus_is_rtp
functions.description: Quick check to determine if a buffer likely contains an RTP packet (useful for demultiplexing RTP from other protocols). Returns TRUE if it looks like RTP, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to at least len bytes of data.
len should be the number of bytes available in buf.

functions.name: janus_rtp_payload
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the start of the RTP payload, skipping the RTP header and any header extensions. If not a valid RTP packet or payload cannot be determined, returns NULL. If plen is provided, it is set to the payload length in bytes.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet (header, optional extensions, and payload).
len should be the total packet length in bytes.
plen, if non-NULL, must be writable to store the payload length.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_get_id
functions.description: Scans an SDP for an extmap declaration and returns the ID associated with the specified RTP header extension namespace. Returns -1 if not found.
requirements: sdp must be a NUL-terminated SDP string to parse.
extension must be a NUL-terminated RTP header extension namespace string (e.g., one of the JANUS_RTP_EXTMAP_* constants).

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_get_from_id
functions.description: Scans an SDP and returns the RTP header extension namespace (URI) associated with the given extmap ID, or NULL if not found. Only extensions known/defined in rtp.h are considered.
requirements: sdp must be a NUL-terminated SDP string to parse.
id should be the extmap ID to look up (typically a small positive integer).

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_audio_level
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_audio_level(char *buf, int len, int id, gboolean *vad, int *level);
functions.description: Parses the ssrc-audio-level RTP header extension (RFC 6464). On success, writes the VAD bit and audio level (dBov, 0=max, 127=min). Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise. Note: browsers often set VAD to 1, so it's unreliable; use the level value instead if needed.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the ssrc-audio-level extension ID to search for.
vad must be a valid pointer to store the VAD flag.
level must be a valid pointer to store the level (0..127).

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_video_orientation
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_video_orientation(char *buf, int len, int id, gboolean *c, gboolean *f, gboolean *r1, gboolean *r0);
functions.description: Parses the video-orientation RTP header extension, extracting the Camera (C), Flip (F), and Rotation bits (R1, R0). Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the video-orientation extension ID to search for.
c, f, r1, r0 must be valid pointers to store the extracted bits.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_playout_delay
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_playout_delay(char *buf, int len, int id, uint16_t *min_delay, uint16_t *max_delay);
functions.description: Parses the playout-delay RTP header extension, returning the minimum and maximum playout delay values. Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the playout-delay extension ID to search for.
min_delay and max_delay must be writable pointers to receive the values.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_mid
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_mid(char *buf, int len, int id, char *sdes_item, int sdes_len);
functions.description: Parses the sdes:mid RTP header extension and writes the MID string to the provided buffer. Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the sdes:mid extension ID to search for.
sdes_item must point to a writable buffer of size sdes_len bytes.
sdes_len specifies the size of the output buffer and must be positive.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_rid
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_rid(char *buf, int len, int id, char *sdes_item, int sdes_len);
functions.description: Parses the rtp-stream-id RTP header extension and writes the RID string to the provided buffer. Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the rtp-stream-id extension ID to search for.
sdes_item must point to a writable buffer of size sdes_len bytes.
sdes_len specifies the size of the output buffer and must be positive.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_dependency_desc
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_dependency_desc(char *buf, int len, int id, uint8_t *dd_item, int *dd_len);
functions.description: Parses the AV1 Dependency Descriptor RTP header extension and copies its raw content into dd_item. On return, dd_len holds the size of the data copied. Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the dependency descriptor extension ID to search for.
dd_item must point to a writable buffer with capacity indicated by *dd_len on input.
dd_len must be a valid pointer; on input it specifies buffer capacity, and on success it is updated with the size of the data.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_abs_send_time
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_abs_send_time(char *buf, int len, int id, uint32_t *abs_ts);
functions.description: Parses the abs-send-time RTP header extension and writes the parsed 24-bit fixed-point timestamp into abs_ts. Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the abs-send-time extension ID to search for.
abs_ts must be a valid pointer to store the parsed value.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_set_abs_send_time
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_set_abs_send_time(char *buf, int len, int id, uint32_t abs_ts);
functions.description: Finds the abs-send-time RTP header extension in the packet and sets it to the provided value. Returns 0 if found and set, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet and must be writable.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the abs-send-time extension ID to search for.
abs_ts is the value to set for the extension.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_abs_capture_time
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_abs_capture_time(char *buf, int len, int id, uint64_t *abs_ts);
functions.description: Parses the abs-capture-time RTP header extension and writes the parsed timestamp into abs_ts. Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the abs-capture-time extension ID to search for.
abs_ts must be a valid pointer to store the parsed value.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_set_abs_capture_time
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_set_abs_capture_time(char *buf, int len, int id, uint64_t abs_ts);
functions.description: Finds the abs-capture-time RTP header extension in the packet and sets it to the provided value. Returns 0 if found and set, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet and must be writable.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the abs-capture-time extension ID to search for.
abs_ts is the value to set for the extension.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_transport_wide_cc
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_transport_wide_cc(char *buf, int len, int id, uint16_t *transSeqNum);
functions.description: Parses the transport-wide congestion control (transport-wide sequence number) RTP header extension and returns the sequence number in transSeqNum. Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the transport-wide-cc extension ID to search for.
transSeqNum must be a valid pointer to store the parsed sequence number.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_set_transport_wide_cc
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_set_transport_wide_cc(char *buf, int len, int id, uint16_t transSeqNum);
functions.description: Finds the transport-wide-cc RTP header extension in the packet and sets its sequence number to the provided value. Returns 0 if found and set, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet and must be writable.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the transport-wide-cc extension ID to search for.
transSeqNum is the value to set for the extension.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_video_layers_allocation
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_parse_video_layers_allocation(char *buf, int len, int id, int8_t *spatial_layers, int8_t *temporal_layers);
functions.description: Parses the video layers allocation RTP header extension and returns the advertised spatial and temporal layers. Returns 0 if found, -1 otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the video-layers-allocation extension ID to search for.
spatial_layers and temporal_layers must be valid pointers to store the parsed values.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_extension_replace_id
functions.signature: int janus_rtp_header_extension_replace_id(char *buf, int len, int id, int new_id);
functions.description: Searches for an RTP header extension with the specified ID and replaces its ID with new_id (e.g., converting repaired-rtp-stream-id to rtp-stream-id after RTX). Returns 0 if the extension was found (and updated), negative otherwise.
requirements: buf should point to len bytes of an RTP packet and must be writable.
len should be the total RTP packet length.
id is the current extension ID to search for.
new_id is the new ID to set for the found extension.

functions.name: janus_rtp_switching_context_reset
functions.description: Initializes or resets all fields of an RTP switching context to their defaults, to (re)start coherent seq/timestamp tracking across SSRC changes.
requirements: context must be a valid pointer to a janus_rtp_switching_context structure to be reset.

functions.name: janus_rtp_header_update
functions.signature: void janus_rtp_header_update(janus_rtp_header *header, janus_rtp_switching_context *context, gboolean video, int step);
functions.description: Updates an RTP header in place using the provided switching context to maintain coherent sequence numbers and timestamps across SSRC changes. The step parameter is deprecated.
requirements: header must be a valid pointer to an RTP header to update.
context must be a valid pointer to an initialized switching context.
video indicates whether this packet is video (TRUE) or audio (FALSE).
step is deprecated and should not be relied upon.

functions.name: janus_rtp_skew_compensate_audio
functions.description: Compensates for audio source clock skew using the switching context and the packet arrival monotonic time. Returns 0 if no compensation was applied, a negative value (-N) if N packets should be dropped, or a positive value (N) if a jump of N sequence numbers was performed.
requirements: header must point to a valid RTP header to potentially adjust.
context must be a valid pointer to a switching context that tracks skew.
now must be the packet arrival monotonic time (unit not explicitly specified; follows implementation expectations).

functions.name: janus_rtp_skew_compensate_video
functions.description: Compensates for video source clock skew using the switching context and the packet arrival monotonic time. Returns 0 if no compensation was applied, a negative value (-N) if N packets should be dropped, or a positive value (N) if a jump of N sequence numbers was performed.
requirements: header must point to a valid RTP header to potentially adjust.
context must be a valid pointer to a switching context that tracks skew.
now must be the packet arrival monotonic time (unit not explicitly specified; follows implementation expectations).

functions.name: janus_av1_svc_context_reset
functions.description: Initializes or resets an AV1 SVC context, clearing tracked templates and layer information.
requirements: context must be a valid pointer to a janus_av1_svc_context to be reset.

functions.name: janus_av1_svc_context_process_dd
functions.signature: gboolean janus_av1_svc_context_process_dd(janus_av1_svc_context *context, uint8_t *dd, int dd_len, uint8_t *template_id, uint8_t *ebit);
functions.description: Processes an AV1 Dependency Descriptor payload, updating the AV1 SVC context (templates and available layers). On success, returns TRUE and provides the referenced template ID and whether the packet is end-of-frame (ebit). Returns FALSE if the packet should be dropped.
requirements: context must be a valid pointer to an initialized AV1 SVC context.
dd must point to dd_len bytes containing the Dependency Descriptor payload.
dd_len must be the size in bytes of the DD payload.
template_id and ebit must be valid pointers to receive the parsed values.

functions.name: janus_rtp_simulcasting_context_reset
functions.description: Initializes or resets a simulcasting context, clearing state related to substreams, temporal layers, extension IDs, and flags.
requirements: context must be a valid pointer to a janus_rtp_simulcasting_context to be reset.

functions.name: janus_rtp_simulcasting_prepare
functions.description: Initializes simulcast-related information (RIDs and/or SSRCs) from a JSON simulcast object provided by the core. May set the RID RTP extension ID, update SSRCs, and allocate RID strings.
requirements: simulcast should be a valid JSON object containing SSRCs and/or RIDs.
