rid_ext_id, if non-NULL, must be writable to store the RID RTP extension ID.
ssrcs, if non-NULL, must point to writable storage for simulcast SSRCs.
rids, if non-NULL, must be an array of char* slots; items may be allocated by this function and must later be freed via janus_rtp_simulcasting_cleanup.

functions.name: janus_rtp_simulcasting_cleanup
functions.description: Cleans up simulcast-related information previously prepared (RID extension ID, SSRCs, and/or allocated RID strings). If a mutex is provided, it must be acquired before cleaning up.
requirements: rid_ext_id, if non-NULL, must be writable to clear the value.
ssrcs, if non-NULL, must be writable to clear SSRCs.
rids, if non-NULL, must be an array of char*; any allocated items will be freed and set to NULL.
If rid_mutex is provided (non-NULL), it must be acquired before calling this function (as explicitly stated).

functions.name: janus_rtp_simulcasting_context_process_rtp
functions.signature: gboolean janus_rtp_simulcasting_context_process_rtp(janus_rtp_simulcasting_context *context, char *buf, int len, uint8_t *dd_content, int dd_len, uint32_t *ssrcs, char **rids, janus_videocodec vcodec, janus_rtp_switching_context *sc, janus_mutex *rid_mutex);
functions.description: Processes an RTP packet for simulcasting, deciding whether to relay or drop it while updating context (substream/layer state and related flags). On each call, changed_substream, changed_temporal, and need_pli are reset and then updated to reflect decisions. Returns TRUE to relay, FALSE to drop.
requirements: context must be a valid pointer to an initialized simulcasting context.
buf must point to len bytes of an RTP packet (header, extensions, payload).
len is the total length of the RTP packet in bytes.
dd_content, if provided, must point to dd_len bytes of Dependency Descriptor data.
ssrcs may be updated if RIDs are involved; must be a valid pointer if provided.
rids may be read; if provided and shared, rid_mutex should be acquired before access (as documented).
vcodec must indicate the video codec of the RTP payload.
sc, if provided, should reference a valid RTP switching context (needed for VP8 temporal layer dropping).
rid_mutex, if provided, should be acquired before reading rids.

functions.name: janus_rtp_svc_context_reset
functions.description: Initializes or resets a VP9/AV1 SVC context, clearing tracked spatial/temporal layer state, timestamps, and related flags.
requirements: context must be a valid pointer to a janus_rtp_svc_context to be reset.

functions.name: janus_rtp_svc_context_process_rtp
functions.signature: gboolean janus_rtp_svc_context_process_rtp(janus_rtp_svc_context *context, char *buf, int len, uint8_t *dd_content, int dd_len, janus_videocodec vcodec, janus_vp9_svc_info *info, janus_rtp_switching_context *sc);
functions.description: Processes an RTP packet for SVC (e.g., VP9-SVC and AV1 via DD), deciding whether to relay or drop while updating spatial/temporal layer decisions and flags. Returns TRUE to relay, FALSE to drop.
requirements: context must be a valid pointer to an initialized SVC context.
buf must point to len bytes of an RTP packet (header, extensions, payload).
len is the total length of the RTP packet in bytes.
dd_content, if provided, must point to dd_len bytes of Dependency Descriptor data.
vcodec must specify the video codec of the RTP payload.
info, if provided, should contain parsed VP9-SVC information.
sc, if provided, should reference a valid RTP switching context.

functions.name: srtp_crypto_get_random
functions.description: Generates cryptographically secure random bytes and writes them into the provided buffer. In builds with libsrtp2, this helper is declared here and typically sources randomness via OpenSSL; with older libsrtp it is a macro alias to crypto_get_random with an equivalent signature. Use it to fill SRTP master keys/salts before creating SRTP sessions. Return value semantics are not documented in this header; treat non-zero/negative returns as implementation-defined errors.
requirements: key must be a valid, writable pointer to a buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be a non-negative integer; zero is allowed to request no bytes.
Callers should check the return value for failure; exact success/error codes are not documented here.
Function availability varies by build: with libsrtp2 it is provided here; with older libsrtp it maps to crypto_get_random.

functions.name: janus_srtp_error_str
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing a libsrtp error code. Use it to log or display the meaning of SRTP-related errors returned by libsrtp APIs or wrappers within Janus.
requirements: error should be a libsrtp error code (srtp_err_status_t or its integer value).
The returned pointer refers to a string owned by the library; callers must not modify or free it.
If an unknown code is provided, the returned string content is unspecified (likely a generic/unknown message).

functions.name: janus_sdp_parse_mtype
functions.description: Parses an SDP m-line media type string (e.g., "audio", "video", "application") into a janus_sdp_mtype enum value for quick comparison/branching.
requirements: type: should be a valid C string; pass a string like "audio", "video", or "application".
Returns JANUS_SDP_OTHER for unsupported types (implied by enum presence).

functions.name: janus_sdp_mtype_str
functions.description: Returns the canonical string corresponding to a janus_sdp_mtype value, or NULL if the value is invalid.
requirements: type must be a valid janus_sdp_mtype value for a non-NULL result.
The returned pointer is not owned by the caller and must not be freed.

functions.name: janus_sdp_parse_mdirection
functions.description: Parses an SDP direction attribute string (e.g., "sendrecv", "sendonly", "recvonly", "inactive") into a janus_sdp_mdirection enum value. Returns JANUS_SDP_INVALID when parsing fails.
requirements: direction: should be a valid C string with a supported direction keyword.

functions.name: janus_sdp_mdirection_str
functions.description: Returns the string representation of a janus_sdp_mdirection value, or NULL if invalid.
requirements: direction must be a valid janus_sdp_mdirection value for a non-NULL result.
The returned string must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: janus_sdp_find_preferred_codec
functions.signature: void janus_sdp_find_preferred_codec(janus_sdp *sdp, janus_sdp_mtype type, int index, const char **codec);
functions.description: Finds the locally preferred codec (per Janus preference, not the SDP order) for the specified media type and m-line in an SDP, provided the m-line isn’t disabled (port=0 or direction=inactive). Writes the result to codec as a static string.
requirements: sdp must point to a valid janus_sdp instance.
type must be JANUS_SDP_AUDIO or JANUS_SDP_VIDEO to make sense.
index selects the m-line of the given type; use -1 to pick the first matching m-line.
codec: must be a valid pointer to receive the result; the stored value points to static storage and must not be freed.

functions.name: janus_sdp_find_first_codec
functions.signature: void janus_sdp_find_first_codec(janus_sdp *sdp, janus_sdp_mtype type, int index, const char **codec);
functions.description: Returns the first codec listed in the specified SDP m-line (regardless of local preference), provided the m-line isn’t disabled. Writes the result to codec as a static string.
requirements: sdp must be a valid janus_sdp.
type must indicate audio or video.
index selects the m-line; use -1 for the first matching m-line.
codec must be a non-NULL output parameter; the returned value is static and must not be freed.

functions.name: janus_sdp_match_preferred_codec
functions.description: Checks whether a codec name matches one of Janus’ preferred codecs for the given media type, returning the canonical preferred codec name if matched, otherwise NULL. The returned string is constant.
requirements: type indicates the media class to match (audio/video).
codec must be a valid codec name string.
Do not free the returned string; it is a constant if non-NULL.

functions.name: janus_sdp_mline_create
functions.signature: janus_sdp_mline *janus_sdp_mline_create(janus_sdp_mtype type, guint16 port, const char *proto, janus_sdp_mdirection direction);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a janus_sdp_mline with the specified media type, port, transport profile, and direction. For non-OTHER types, type_str is auto-set from type; for JANUS_SDP_OTHER, type_str is not allocated and must be provided by the caller later.
requirements: type_str is NOT allocated when type == JANUS_SDP_OTHER; caller must set mline->type_str appropriately.
proto must be a valid transport/profile string (e.g., "RTP/SAVPF").
Returned pointer must be released with janus_sdp_mline_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: janus_sdp_mline_destroy
functions.description: Releases resources held by a janus_sdp_mline. It does not remove the m-line from any janus_sdp container; callers must unlink it from sdp->m_lines separately before destroying.
requirements: mline must be a valid janus_sdp_mline pointer created by janus_sdp_mline_create.
This function does NOT remove the m-line from a janus_sdp; caller must remove it from the SDP structure before or after destroying.

functions.name: janus_sdp_mline_find
functions.description: Finds and returns the first m-line of the specified media type within an SDP. Intended mainly for simpler (non-multistream) scenarios.
requirements: sdp must be a valid janus_sdp object.
Returns the first matching m-line if any; may return NULL if none found.

functions.name: janus_sdp_mline_find_by_index
functions.description: Looks up an m-line by its index within the SDP and returns it, or NULL if not found.
requirements: sdp must be valid.
index must correspond to an existing m-line to get a non-NULL result.

functions.name: janus_sdp_mline_remove
functions.description: Removes the first m-line of the specified type from the given SDP. Returns 0 on success, negative value on failure.
requirements: sdp must be valid.
Only the first m-line of the requested type is removed (explicit behavior).
Caller should manage any further cleanup tied to the removed m-line as appropriate.

functions.name: janus_sdp_attribute_create
functions.description: Allocates a new SDP attribute (a=) with the specified name and a printf-style formatted value constructed from the variadic arguments.
requirements: name must be a valid attribute name string (e.g., "rtpmap").
value is a printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.
Returned pointer must be freed with janus_sdp_attribute_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: janus_sdp_attribute_destroy
functions.description: Frees a janus_sdp_attribute. This does not remove the attribute from any attribute list; the caller must unlink it first.
requirements: attr must be a valid janus_sdp_attribute pointer created by janus_sdp_attribute_create.
This function does NOT remove the attribute from global or m-line lists; caller must unlink it before/after destroying.

functions.name: janus_sdp_attribute_add_to_mline
functions.description: Appends an attribute to an m-line’s attribute list. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: mline must be a valid janus_sdp_mline.
attr must be a valid janus_sdp_attribute (typically created with janus_sdp_attribute_create).

functions.name: janus_sdp_parse
functions.description: Parses a textual SDP into a janus_sdp structure. On failure, returns NULL and, if an error buffer is provided, writes a reason into it.
requirements: sdp must be a valid SDP string.
error may be NULL; if non-NULL, errlen must specify the buffer size to avoid overflow.
On error, check for NULL return and optionally inspect error buffer for the reason.

functions.name: janus_sdp_remove_payload_type
functions.signature: int janus_sdp_remove_payload_type(janus_sdp *sdp, int index, int pt);
functions.description: Removes all occurrences of a payload type (pt) and related attributes (rtpmap, fmtp, etc.) from the specified m-line. Returns 0 on success, negative on failure.
requirements: sdp must be valid.
index selects the m-line; use -1 for the first matching m-line.
pt must be a valid payload type integer present in the chosen m-line to succeed.

functions.name: janus_sdp_write
functions.description: Serializes a janus_sdp object into a newly allocated SDP string representation. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: sdp must be a valid janus_sdp object.
The returned string is heap-allocated; the caller must free it (e.g., with g_free) when done.

functions.name: janus_sdp_new
functions.description: Creates a new janus_sdp with some fields initialized from the provided session name and IP address. If name or address are NULL, defaults are used. This allocates o_addr, s_name, and c_addr.
requirements: If you later replace o_addr, s_name, or c_addr, you must free the originally allocated strings first (per note).
Returned janus_sdp must be destroyed with janus_sdp_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: janus_sdp_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a janus_sdp and releases all associated resources.
requirements: sdp must be a janus_sdp previously created (e.g., by janus_sdp_new, janus_sdp_parse, or janus_sdp_generate_*).

functions.name: janus_sdp_oa_type_str
functions.description: Returns the string name of a janus_sdp_oa_type enumerator (used for offer/answer generation properties).
requirements: type must be a valid janus_sdp_oa_type to get a meaningful string.
Returned string must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: janus_sdp_generate_offer
functions.description: Builds a janus_sdp offer using a sequence of (property, value) variadic arguments terminated by JANUS_SDP_OA_DONE. Properties like JANUS_SDP_OA_MLINE, JANUS_SDP_OA_DIRECTION, JANUS_SDP_OA_CODEC, etc., control media sections, directions, codecs, payload types, extensions, and more. If not specified, the default is to not offer any media.
requirements: Arguments must be a sequence of janus_sdp_oa_type followed by the expected value(s) for each, terminated by JANUS_SDP_OA_DONE.
JANUS_SDP_OA_MLINE must precede details for that media section when adding streams.
name and address may be NULL to use defaults.
Returns a janus_sdp that must be freed with janus_sdp_destroy.

functions.name: janus_sdp_generate_offer_mline
functions.description: Adds a single m-line to an existing offer using the same variadic (property, value) pairs as janus_sdp_generate_offer. The first argument MUST be JANUS_SDP_OA_MLINE with the media type. Defaults: audio->Opus PT 111; video->VP8 PT 96; direction sendrecv.
requirements: offer must be a valid janus_sdp created for offering.
Variadic list must start with JANUS_SDP_OA_MLINE and be terminated with JANUS_SDP_OA_DONE.
Returns 0 on success, negative on failure.

functions.name: janus_sdp_generate_answer
functions.description: Creates a skeletal SDP answer for a given offer: copies overall structure and m-lines but initially rejects all m-lines. Use janus_sdp_generate_answer_mline to configure each m-line’s acceptance, direction, codec, etc. Default, if unspecified, is to accept everything as sendrecv.
requirements: offer must be a valid janus_sdp offer to respond to.
After creation, iterate offer m-lines and call janus_sdp_generate_answer_mline for each to build the final answer.
Returns a janus_sdp to be freed with janus_sdp_destroy.

functions.name: janus_sdp_generate_answer_mline
functions.description: Responds to a single offered m-line using the same variadic property/value scheme as offer generation. The first argument MUST be JANUS_SDP_OA_MLINE (media type). For example, you can accept audio as recvonly and choose Opus. Returns 0 on success, negative on failure.
requirements: offer must be the original janus_sdp offer.
answer must be the janus_sdp answer being built.
offered must be a janus_sdp_mline from the offer to which you are responding.
Variadic list must start with JANUS_SDP_OA_MLINE and end with JANUS_SDP_OA_DONE.

functions.name: janus_sdp_get_codec_pt
functions.signature: int janus_sdp_get_codec_pt(janus_sdp *sdp, int index, const char *codec);
functions.description: Returns the payload type number associated with a codec in the specified m-line, ignoring codec profiles. On success returns the PT, otherwise -1.
requirements: sdp must be valid.
index selects the m-line; -1 means first matching m-line.
codec must be a codec name string (e.g., "opus", "vp8").

functions.name: janus_sdp_get_codec_pt_full
functions.signature: int janus_sdp_get_codec_pt_full(janus_sdp *sdp, int index, const char *codec, const char *profile);
functions.description: Returns the payload type number for a codec in the specified m-line considering a profile hint (currently applies to VP9 and H.264). If the codec exists but the specified profile isn’t found, returns -1.
requirements: sdp must be valid.
index selects the m-line; -1 means first matching m-line.
codec must be a codec name string.
profile should be a supported profile string for codecs that use profiles (VP9, H.264).

functions.name: janus_sdp_get_codec_name
functions.signature: const char *janus_sdp_get_codec_name(janus_sdp *sdp, int index, int pt);
functions.description: Looks up the codec name associated with a payload type in the specified m-line. Returns the codec name string or NULL if not found.
requirements: sdp must be valid.
index selects the m-line; -1 for first matching m-line.
pt is the payload type to query.
Returned string must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: janus_sdp_get_rtpmap_codec
functions.description: Extracts the codec name from an rtpmap string like "VP8/90000" and returns it (e.g., "vp8"). Returns NULL if not recognized.
requirements: rtpmap must be a valid rtpmap string of the form "<codec>/<clock>[/<channels>]".
Returned string must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: janus_sdp_get_codec_rtpmap
functions.description: Returns the rtpmap string for a given codec name (e.g., for "opus" returns "opus/48000/2"), or NULL if unknown.
requirements: codec must be a valid codec name string.
Returned string must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: janus_sdp_get_fmtp
functions.signature: const char *janus_sdp_get_fmtp(janus_sdp *sdp, int index, int pt);
functions.description: Returns the fmtp value associated with a payload type in the specified m-line, or NULL if not present.
requirements: sdp must be valid.
index selects the m-line; -1 selects the first matching m-line.
pt must be an existing payload type in the m-line to obtain a non-NULL result.
Returned string must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: janus_sdp_get_video_profile
functions.description: Parses a video fmtp string and extracts the H.264 or VP9 profile, returning a newly allocated profile string, or NULL if not found. Caller must free the returned string.
requirements: codec must indicate the video codec (H.264 or VP9 supported per note).
fmtp must be the fmtp value to parse for profile parameters.
The returned profile string is allocated and must be freed by the caller.

functions.name: janus_sdp_get_opusred_pt
functions.description: Returns the payload type for opus/red in the specified m-line if present, or -1 otherwise.
requirements: sdp must be valid.
index selects the m-line; -1 selects the first matching m-line.

functions.name: janus_network_prepare_device_query
functions.signature: int janus_network_prepare_device_query(const char *user_value, const janus_network_query_options query_mode, janus_network_query_config *query)
functions.description: Initializes a janus_network_query_config to look up a network device by name and/or IP address, according to the provided mode mask. Use when you want to search interfaces by a user-provided string that may be a device name or IPv4/IPv6 address.
requirements: user_value must be non-NULL.
query must be non-NULL.
query_mode should be a valid combination of janus_network_query_options flags.
If matching by name is disabled in query_mode, user_value must be a valid IPv4/IPv6 address compatible with the enabled address family flags, otherwise the function fails with -EINVAL.
Returns 0 on success, or -EINVAL on invalid arguments or when user_value is not a valid IP while name matching is disabled.

functions.name: janus_network_prepare_device_query_default
functions.description: Initializes a janus_network_query_config using default options (accept any supported match type: name, IPv4, or IPv6).
requirements: user_value must be non-NULL.
query must be non-NULL.
Returns 0 on success, or -EINVAL if any argument is NULL.

functions.name: janus_network_query_devices
functions.signature: const struct ifaddrs *janus_network_query_devices(const struct ifaddrs *ifas, const janus_network_query_config *query)
functions.description: Searches the ifaddrs list for the first interface that matches the provided query; pass the returned_node->ifa_next on subsequent calls to find additional matches.
requirements: ifas should point to the head (or a node) of a list returned by getifaddrs.
query should be a valid, initialized janus_network_query_config (e.g., from janus_network_prepare_device_query or _default).
Returns a pointer to the first matching struct ifaddrs, or NULL if none found.

functions.name: janus_network_get_devices_ipv4
functions.signature: int janus_network_get_devices_ipv4(const struct ifaddrs *ifa, const janus_network_query_config *query, struct in_addr *result)
functions.description: Copies the IPv4 address from a matching interface description into result. Use after locating an interface with janus_network_query_devices.
requirements: ifa must be non-NULL and describe an interface with an IPv4 address.
query must be non-NULL and correspond to an IPv4 configuration.
result must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for struct in_addr.
Returns 0 on success, -EINVAL if any argument is NULL or if the interface/query do not correspond to IPv4.

functions.name: janus_network_get_devices_ipv6
functions.signature: int janus_network_get_devices_ipv6(const struct ifaddrs *ifa, const janus_network_query_config *query, struct in6_addr *result)
functions.description: Copies the IPv6 address from a matching interface description into result. Use after locating an interface with janus_network_query_devices.
requirements: ifa must be non-NULL and describe an interface with an IPv6 address.
query must be non-NULL and correspond to an IPv6 configuration.
result must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for struct in6_addr.
Returns 0 on success, -EINVAL if any argument is NULL or if the interface/query do not correspond to IPv6.

functions.name: janus_network_get_device_address
functions.description: Copies the IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) from an interface description into a tagged janus_network_address.
requirements: ifa must be non-NULL and correspond to an IP (AF_INET or AF_INET6) address.
result must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for janus_network_address.
Returns 0 on success, or -EINVAL if any argument is NULL or the interface does not correspond to an IP address.

functions.name: janus_network_address_nullify
functions.description: Sets a janus_network_address to a null/nil value so it represents no address.
requirements: a may be NULL; if NULL, nothing is done.

functions.name: janus_network_address_is_null
functions.description: Checks whether a janus_network_address is null-valued (as set by janus_network_address_nullify). Returns positive if null-valued, 0 otherwise.
requirements: a should be non-NULL.

functions.name: janus_network_address_from_sockaddr
functions.description: Converts a struct sockaddr (AF_INET or AF_INET6) into a janus_network_address.
requirements: s must be non-NULL and point to a valid struct sockaddr for AF_INET or AF_INET6.
a must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
Returns 0 on success, or -EINVAL otherwise.

functions.name: janus_network_address_to_string_buffer
functions.description: Converts a janus_network_address into a buffer that can be used to extract a human-readable IP string (via janus_network_address_string_from_buffer).
requirements: a must be non-NULL and contain a valid AF_INET or AF_INET6 address.
buf must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for janus_network_address_string_buffer.
Returns 0 on success, or -EINVAL if any argument is NULL.

functions.name: janus_network_address_string_buffer_nullify
functions.description: Sets a janus_network_address_string_buffer to a null/nil value so it represents no address string.
requirements: b may be NULL; if NULL, nothing is done.

functions.name: janus_network_address_string_buffer_is_null
functions.description: Checks whether a janus_network_address_string_buffer is null-valued. Returns positive if null-valued, 0 otherwise.
requirements: b should be non-NULL.

functions.name: janus_network_address_string_from_buffer
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the human-readable IP string contained in a janus_network_address_string_buffer, or NULL if the buffer is invalid or NULL.
requirements: b may be NULL; returns NULL if b is invalid or NULL.
The returned pointer refers to memory within b; b must remain valid while using the returned string.

functions.name: janus_network_string_is_valid_address
functions.description: Validates whether user_value is a syntactically valid IP address of the specified type (IPv4, IPv6, or any IP). Returns positive if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: addr_type should be one of janus_network_query_options_ipv4, janus_network_query_options_ipv6, or janus_network_query_options_any_ip.
user_value must be non-NULL.

functions.name: janus_network_string_to_address
functions.description: Parses an IP address string into a janus_network_address of the requested type (IPv4, IPv6, or any IP).
requirements: addr_type should be one of janus_network_query_options_ipv4, janus_network_query_options_ipv6, or janus_network_query_options_any_ip.
user_value must be non-NULL and contain a valid IP address compatible with addr_type.
result must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
Returns 0 on success, -EINVAL otherwise.

functions.name: janus_network_lookup_interface
functions.signature: int janus_network_lookup_interface(const struct ifaddrs *ifas, const char *iface, janus_network_address *result)
functions.description: Resolves an interface name or IP address to a janus_network_address by consulting the provided interfaces list.
requirements: ifas should point to a list returned by getifaddrs.
iface must be non-NULL and be either an interface name or an IP address string.
result must be non-NULL and point to writable storage.
Returns 0 on success, -EINVAL otherwise.

functions.name: janus_network_detect_local_ip
functions.description: Finds a usable local IP address of the requested type (IPv4, IPv6, or any IP) suitable for communication.
requirements: addr_type should be one of janus_network_query_options_ipv4, janus_network_query_options_ipv6, or janus_network_query_options_any_ip.
result must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for janus_network_address.
Returns 0 on success, -EINVAL otherwise.

functions.name: janus_network_detect_local_ip_as_string
functions.description: Returns a newly allocated string with a usable local IP address of the requested type.
requirements: addr_type should be one of janus_network_query_options_ipv4, janus_network_query_options_ipv6, or janus_network_query_options_any_ip.
The returned string is allocated with g_strdup and must be freed by the caller (e.g., with g_free).
Returns a non-NULL string on success, or NULL on error; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: janus_network_resolve_address
functions.description: Resolves a host string into a sockaddr_storage using inet_pton for numeric addresses or getaddrinfo otherwise; this call is synchronous and may block waiting for DNS.
requirements: host must be non-NULL.
address must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for struct sockaddr_storage.
May block due to DNS resolution; avoid calling on time-sensitive threads.
Returns 0 on success, a negative integer otherwise.

functions.name: janus_mark_started
functions.description: Marks the time when Janus started. Used internally to allow returning monotonic time normalized to the Janus start time.

functions.name: janus_get_monotonic_time_internal
functions.description: Returns the system monotonic time. Provided for environments where g_get_monotonic_time may be unavailable (pre-GLib 2.28).

functions.name: janus_get_monotonic_time
functions.description: Returns the system monotonic time normalized from the Janus start time (i.e., relative to when janus_mark_started was called). Useful for relative time measurements.

functions.name: janus_get_real_time
functions.description: Returns the system real time. Provided for environments where g_get_real_time may be unavailable (pre-GLib 2.28).

functions.name: janus_string_replace
functions.signature: char *janus_string_replace(char *message, const char *old_string, const char *new_string) G_GNUC_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT;
functions.description: Replaces occurrences of old_string with new_string in message, possibly reallocating the storage. If the original buffer is too short, it may be freed and a new buffer returned. The returned pointer is the updated string.
requirements: Caller must use the returned pointer after the call; the original message pointer may be invalidated.
The message passed in may be freed by this function; pass a dynamically allocated, freeable buffer.
old_string and new_string should be valid, NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: janus_strlcat
functions.signature: size_t janus_strlcat(char *dest, const char *src, size_t dest_size);
functions.description: Appends src to the end of NUL-terminated dest, writing at most dest_size bytes in total. Logs an error if truncation occurred. Returns the size of the attempted result; if it is >= dest_size, truncation occurred.
requirements: dest must point to a buffer of size dest_size and already contain a NUL-terminated string.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
dest_size must be the total size of the destination buffer in bytes (not the current string length).

functions.name: janus_strlcat_fast
functions.signature: int janus_strlcat_fast(char *dest, const char *src, size_t dest_size, size_t *offset);
functions.description: Appends src to dest using a faster memccpy-based approach. The offset parameter is both input and output and is updated to the new end position. Returns 0 on success, negative on error, and logs an error if truncation occurred.
requirements: dest must point to a buffer of size dest_size and already contain a NUL-terminated string.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
offset must point to the current append position within dest and is updated on return.
dest_size must be the total size of the destination buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_is_true
functions.description: Parses a string configuration value and returns TRUE if it represents a true value. Recognizes yes/YES/true/TRUE/"1"; otherwise returns FALSE.

functions.name: janus_strcmp_const_time
functions.description: Constant-time comparison of two strings. Returns TRUE if the strings are the same, FALSE otherwise. Intended to avoid timing attacks when comparing secrets.

functions.name: janus_random_uint32
functions.description: Generates a random 32-bit unsigned integer. Falls back to a non-cryptographically safe PRNG if the crypto RAND_bytes() call fails.

functions.name: janus_random_uint64_full
functions.description: Generates a random 64-bit unsigned integer (full 64 bits). Falls back to a non-cryptographically safe PRNG if the crypto RAND_bytes() call fails.

functions.name: janus_random_uint64
functions.description: Generates a random unsigned integer that fits safely in JavaScript’s Number type (52 significant bits). Named for backward compatibility. Falls back to a non-cryptographically safe PRNG if the crypto RAND_bytes() call fails.

functions.name: janus_random_uuid
functions.description: Generates a random UUID string. Falls back to a non-cryptographically safe PRNG if the crypto RAND_bytes() call fails. The returned string must be deallocated with g_free.
requirements: Caller must free the returned string with g_free.

functions.name: janus_uint64_dup
functions.description: Allocates and returns a heap-allocated copy of a guint64 value, useful for using guint64 keys in GHashTable without lifetime issues.

functions.name: janus_uint64_hash
functions.description: Hashes a guint64 number to another guint64 number. Currently used for event handlers.

functions.name: janus_string_to_uint8
functions.description: Converts a string to a uint8_t. Returns 0 on success, negative on error (e.g., -ERANGE if out of range). On error, the output value should be ignored.
requirements: str must be a valid numeric string representation for the intended range.
num must be a valid pointer to receive the result.
If the function returns an error, the value pointed to by num must be ignored.

functions.name: janus_string_to_uint16
functions.description: Converts a string to a uint16_t. Returns 0 on success, negative on error (e.g., -ERANGE if out of range). On error, the output value should be ignored.
requirements: str must be a valid numeric string representation for the intended range.
num must be a valid pointer to receive the result.
If the function returns an error, the value pointed to by num must be ignored.

functions.name: janus_string_to_uint32
functions.description: Converts a string to a uint32_t. Returns 0 on success, negative on error (e.g., -ERANGE if out of range). On error, the output value should be ignored.
requirements: str must be a valid numeric string representation for the intended range.
num must be a valid pointer to receive the result.
If the function returns an error, the value pointed to by num must be ignored.

functions.name: janus_flags_reset
functions.description: Resets a janus_flags bitset container (gsize-typed) to the default (cleared) state.
requirements: flags must be a valid pointer to a janus_flags variable.

functions.name: janus_flags_set
functions.description: Sets the specified flag bit in a janus_flags container.
requirements: flags must be a valid pointer to a janus_flags variable.

functions.name: janus_flags_clear
functions.description: Clears the specified flag bit in a janus_flags container.
requirements: flags must be a valid pointer to a janus_flags variable.

functions.name: janus_flags_is_set
functions.description: Checks whether a specific flag bit is set in a janus_flags container.
requirements: flags must be a valid pointer to a janus_flags variable.

functions.name: janus_mkdir
functions.description: Creates a directory at the given path, creating parent directories recursively if needed. Returns an int like mkdir does. Some subdirectories may have been created even if a later failure occurs.
requirements: dir must be a valid path string.
mode specifies file permissions for the new directory.

functions.name: janus_make_absolute_path
functions.description: Converts path relative to base_dir into an absolute path; if path is already absolute, returns a duplicate of it. The result is g_strdup’ed and must be freed with g_free.
requirements: Caller must free the returned string with g_free.
If path is relative, base_dir is used as the prefix.

functions.name: janus_get_codec_pt
functions.description: Parses an SDP to find the payload type (PT) associated with the given codec name. Returns the PT if found, or -1 otherwise.
requirements: sdp must point to a valid SDP string.
codec must be the codec name to look for (case and exact format as expected by the parser).

functions.name: janus_get_codec_from_pt
functions.description: Parses an SDP to find the codec name associated with a given payload type (PT). Returns the codec name if found, or NULL otherwise. Ownership/validity duration of the returned pointer is not documented.
requirements: sdp must point to a valid SDP string.
pt is the payload type to look up.

functions.name: janus_pidfile_create
functions.description: Creates and locks a PID file at the specified path. Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: file must be a valid filesystem path for the PID file.

functions.name: janus_pidfile_remove
functions.description: Unlocks and removes a previously created PID file. Returns 0 on success, negative on error.

functions.name: janus_protected_folder_add
functions.description: Adds a folder to an internal protected list to prevent creating files there (e.g., recordings or pcap dumps).
requirements: folder must be a valid path string.

functions.name: janus_is_folder_protected
functions.description: Checks whether the given path is in the protected folders list. Returns TRUE if protected, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: path must be a valid path string.

functions.name: janus_protected_folders_clear
functions.description: Clears the internal list of protected folders.

functions.name: janus_get_json_type_name
functions.signature: void janus_get_json_type_name(int jtype, unsigned int flags, char *type_name);
functions.description: Writes a human-readable description of a JSON type and constraints into type_name (e.g., "a positive integer"). Required buffer size is 19 characters.
requirements: type_name must point to a buffer of at least 19 characters.
jtype must be a valid json_type value.
flags indicate constraints such as JANUS_JSON_PARAM_REQUIRED, JANUS_JSON_PARAM_POSITIVE, JANUS_JSON_PARAM_NONEMPTY.

functions.name: janus_json_is_valid
functions.signature: gboolean janus_json_is_valid(json_t *val, json_type jtype, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Checks whether a JSON value matches the specified type and constraints. Returns TRUE if valid.
requirements: val must be a valid json_t pointer.
jtype must be a valid json_type value.
flags indicate constraints such as JANUS_JSON_PARAM_POSITIVE or JANUS_JSON_PARAM_NONEMPTY.

functions.name: janus_vp8_is_keyframe
functions.description: Determines whether a VP8 RTP payload is a keyframe. Returns TRUE if keyframe, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_vp9_is_keyframe
functions.description: Determines whether a VP9 RTP payload is a keyframe. Returns TRUE if keyframe, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_h264_is_keyframe
functions.description: Determines whether an H.264 RTP payload contains a keyframe. This checks for presence of an SPS NAL (type 7), as SPS/PPS are needed for browsers to decode. For I-frame detection specifically, use janus_h264_is_i_frame.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_h264_is_i_frame
functions.description: Determines whether an H.264 RTP payload contains an I-frame. Returns TRUE if I-frame, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_h264_is_b_frame
functions.description: Determines whether an H.264 RTP payload contains a B-frame. Returns TRUE if B-frame, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_av1_is_keyframe
functions.description: Determines whether an AV1 RTP payload is a keyframe. Returns TRUE if keyframe, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_h265_is_keyframe
functions.description: Determines whether an H.265 (HEVC) RTP payload is a keyframe. Returns TRUE if keyframe, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_is_keyframe
functions.signature: gboolean janus_is_keyframe(int codec, const char *buffer, int len);
functions.description: Generic keyframe detector that dispatches to the codec-specific helper based on the provided codec type. Returns TRUE if keyframe, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: codec must be a valid janus_videocodec value (as used in the library).
buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.

functions.name: janus_vp8_simulcast_context_reset
functions.description: Initializes or resets a janus_vp8_simulcast_context so that SSRC changes result in coherent PictureID/temporal level handling for VP8 simulcast.
requirements: context must be a valid pointer to a janus_vp8_simulcast_context.

functions.name: janus_vp8_parse_descriptor
functions.signature: int janus_vp8_parse_descriptor(char *buffer, int len, gboolean *m, uint16_t *picid, uint8_t *tl0picidx, uint8_t *tid, uint8_t *y, uint8_t *keyidx);
functions.description: Parses a VP8 payload descriptor from an RTP payload and extracts useful fields (e.g., PictureID, temporal layer indices, etc.). Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.
Output pointers (m, picid, tl0picidx, tid, y, keyidx) should be valid if their values are expected to be filled.

functions.name: janus_vp8_simulcast_descriptor_update
functions.signature: void janus_vp8_simulcast_descriptor_update(char *buffer, int len, janus_vp8_simulcast_context *context, gboolean switched);
functions.description: Updates the VP8 RTP payload descriptor using the provided simulcast context, adjusting headers when a source switch occurs to maintain coherent PictureID/temporal levels.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes to be modified.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.
context must be a valid janus_vp8_simulcast_context.
switched indicates whether a source switch occurred.

functions.name: janus_vp9_parse_svc
functions.signature: int janus_vp9_parse_svc(char *buffer, int len, gboolean *found, janus_vp9_svc_info *info);
functions.description: Parses a VP9 payload descriptor for SVC information (spatial/temporal layer indices and related flags). Sets found to indicate presence of SVC info and fills info. Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.
found must be a valid pointer to receive presence information.
info must point to a janus_vp9_svc_info struct to be filled.

functions.name: janus_red_parse_blocks
functions.description: Parses an RTP payload containing RED (RFC 2198) and returns a GList of janus_red_block entries describing each encapsulated block. The returned list is owned by the caller and must be freed.
requirements: buffer must point to the RTP payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.
Caller must free the returned GList and any associated allocations.

functions.name: janus_red_pack_blocks
functions.description: Packs multiple janus_red_block buffers into a RED RTP payload. Writes into buffer up to len bytes. Returns the size of the RED payload on success, negative on error.
requirements: buffer must point to an output buffer of size len.
len must be sufficient to hold the packed RED payload or the function will fail.
blocks must be a valid GList of janus_red_block entries to pack.

functions.name: janus_red_replace_block_pt
functions.signature: int janus_red_replace_block_pt(char *buffer, int len, int pt);
functions.description: Overwrites all RTP payload types inside RED blocks within the given payload with the specified PT. Returns 0 on success, negative on error.
requirements: buffer must point to the RED payload bytes.
len must specify the length of buffer in bytes.
pt is the RTP payload type to set for all blocks.

functions.name: janus_push_bits
functions.signature: guint32 janus_push_bits(guint32 word, size_t num, guint32 val);
functions.description: Pushes num bits from val at the end of word and returns the new word. Useful for bit-assembly operations.
requirements: num specifies how many bits to push; valid ranges/limits are not documented.

functions.name: janus_set1
functions.signature: void janus_set1(guint8 *data, size_t i, guint8 val);
functions.description: Sets one byte at memory position i within data to val.
requirements: data must point to writable memory with at least i+1 bytes.

functions.name: janus_set2
functions.signature: void janus_set2(guint8 *data, size_t i, guint32 val);
functions.description: Writes two bytes of val at memory position i within data.
requirements: data must point to writable memory with at least i+2 bytes.

functions.name: janus_set3
functions.signature: void janus_set3(guint8 *data, size_t i, guint32 val);
functions.description: Writes three bytes of val at memory position i within data.
requirements: data must point to writable memory with at least i+3 bytes.

functions.name: janus_set4
functions.signature: void janus_set4(guint8 *data, size_t i, guint32 val);
functions.description: Writes four bytes of val at memory position i within data.
requirements: data must point to writable memory with at least i+4 bytes.

functions.name: janus_bitstream_getbit
functions.description: Reads and returns the bit value at the bit offset from the start of a bitstream pointed to by base.
requirements: base must point to a valid bitstream buffer with sufficient size to cover the requested offset.

functions.name: janus_bitstream_getbits
functions.description: Reads num bits starting at *offset from the bitstream base, returns their value, and advances *offset accordingly.
requirements: base must point to a valid bitstream buffer with sufficient size to cover the requested range.
offset must be a valid pointer to the current bit offset and is updated by the function.
num is the number of bits to read; valid ranges are not documented.

functions.name: janus_gzip_compress
functions.signature: size_t janus_gzip_compress(int compression, char *text, size_t tlen, char *compressed, size_t zlen);
functions.description: Compresses a string to gzip using zlib. Returns the size of the compressed data on success, or 0 otherwise. Caller must ensure the output buffer is large enough.
requirements: compression must be between 1 (fastest) and 9 (best compression).
text must point to the input data of length tlen.
compressed must point to an output buffer of size zlen.
zlen must be large enough to hold the compressed data, otherwise the request will fail.

functions.name: janus_refcount_init
functions.description: Macro wrapper that initializes a janus_refcount embedded in an object: sets the counter to 1 and stores the provided finalizer (free) function. At runtime it dispatches to either the debug or non-debug variant based on the global refcount_debug. Use this exactly once when constructing an object that embeds a janus_refcount before sharing it with other threads or callers. Note: this is a macro, not a real function; the free function is invoked when the count drops to 0 and should deallocate the enclosing object (typically via janus_refcount_containerof).
requirements: refp must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized janus_refcount field embedded within an object.
free_fn must be non-null and have the exact signature void (*)(const janus_refcount *); it must correctly finalize and free the enclosing object when invoked at count 0.
Do not call this macro more than once on the same janus_refcount instance unless the object is being reinitialized from scratch.
If this macro is used, the program must provide a definition for the global symbol int refcount_debug (extern in this header), or link with a module that defines it.
The project must provide the JANUS_PRINT macro (used by the debug variants).
Thread-safety of the counter operations relies on GLib's atomic primitives; include and link GLib as required.

functions.name: janus_refcount_init_nodebug
functions.description: Macro that initializes a janus_refcount without extra debug logging. It sets refp->count to 1 and assigns the free function pointer; in REFCOUNT_DEBUG builds it also starts tracking the counter in a global table. Use this when you explicitly want the non-debug path.
requirements: refp must be a valid, non-null pointer to a janus_refcount field.
free_fn must be non-null and have signature void (*)(const janus_refcount *).
Call exactly once per object construction.
In REFCOUNT_DEBUG builds, debug tracking structures (counters and counters_mutex) must be available; this header declares them extern.
Relies on GLib types (gint).

functions.name: janus_refcount_init_debug
functions.description: Macro that initializes a janus_refcount with debug logging (via JANUS_PRINT), sets count to 1, assigns the free function, and in REFCOUNT_DEBUG builds also tracks the counter in a global table. Use for instrumented initialization to trace reference lifetimes.
requirements: refp must be a valid, non-null pointer to a janus_refcount field.
free_fn must be non-null and have signature void (*)(const janus_refcount *).
Call exactly once per object construction.
Requires JANUS_PRINT to be defined and usable at call sites (both in REFCOUNT_DEBUG and non-REFCOUNT_DEBUG branches of this macro).
In REFCOUNT_DEBUG builds, debug tracking structures (counters and counters_mutex) must be available.

functions.name: janus_refcount_increase
functions.description: Macro wrapper that atomically increments the reference count of a previously initialized janus_refcount, dispatching to a debug or non-debug variant based on refcount_debug. Use whenever creating a new retained reference to the object.
requirements: refp must be non-null and must have been initialized via janus_refcount_init(_debug/_nodebug).
Must not be called after the counter has reached 0 and the object has been destroyed.
Relies on GLib atomics (g_atomic_int_inc).

functions.name: janus_refcount_increase_nodebug
functions.description: Macro that atomically increments refp->count without additional logging. Intended for fast-path increments.
requirements: refp must be non-null and previously initialized.
Must not be called after the counter has reached 0 (use-after-free).

functions.name: janus_refcount_increase_debug
functions.description: Macro that logs a message (via JANUS_PRINT) indicating the new reference count and then atomically increments refp->count.
requirements: refp must be non-null and previously initialized.
Requires JANUS_PRINT to be defined and usable.
Must not be called after the counter has reached 0 (use-after-free).

functions.name: janus_refcount_decrease
functions.description: Macro wrapper that atomically decrements the reference count of a janus_refcount, dispatching to debug or non-debug variant based on refcount_debug. If the count reaches 0, it invokes the stored free function to destroy the enclosing object (and, in REFCOUNT_DEBUG builds for the debug variant, untracks it). Use whenever releasing a retained reference.
requirements: refp must be non-null and previously initialized via janus_refcount_init(_debug/_nodebug).
Caller must ensure the number of decreases matches the number of increases plus the initial count of 1 set at initialization, so that the final decrease occurs exactly once.
After this call causes the count to reach 0, the object is considered destroyed and must not be accessed again by the caller or any other code.
The free function must be safe to call in the context/thread where decrease occurs; no additional synchronization is performed besides atomic decrement.

functions.name: janus_refcount_decrease_debug
functions.description: Macro that logs a message (via JANUS_PRINT), atomically decrements refp->count, and if it hits 0 calls the stored free function. In REFCOUNT_DEBUG builds it also removes the counter from the debug tracking table after freeing.
requirements: refp must be non-null and previously initialized.
Requires JANUS_PRINT to be defined and usable.
In REFCOUNT_DEBUG builds, debug tracking structures (counters and counters_mutex) must be available.
Must not be called after the counter has already reached 0.

functions.name: janus_refcount_decrease_nodebug
functions.description: Macro that atomically decrements refp->count without extra logging, and if it reaches 0 invokes the stored free function (and untracks in REFCOUNT_DEBUG builds).
requirements: refp must be non-null and previously initialized.
Must not be called after the counter has already reached 0.
In REFCOUNT_DEBUG builds, debug tracking symbols must be available for the untracking step.

functions.name: janus_text2pcap_packet_string
functions.description: Return a human-readable string for a janus_text2pcap_packet value (e.g., RTP/RTCP/DATA). Useful for logs/diagnostics. The returned string is expected to be a static, null-terminated C string.
requirements: type must be a valid janus_text2pcap_packet enum value (JANUS_TEXT2PCAP_RTP, JANUS_TEXT2PCAP_RTCP, or JANUS_TEXT2PCAP_DATA).
The returned pointer should be treated as read-only; it must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: janus_text2pcap_create
functions.signature: janus_text2pcap *janus_text2pcap_create(const char *dir, const char *filename, int truncate, gboolean text);
functions.description: Create and initialize a text2pcap recorder that dumps RTP/RTCP (and data) either as a text file consumable by text2pcap or directly as a legacy pcap file. If dir is NULL, the current directory is used. If filename is NULL, a random filename is chosen. Pass truncate to limit per-packet bytes (0 for no truncation). Set text to TRUE to write a text dump, or FALSE to write a pcap file. Returns a recorder instance on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: dir may be NULL to use the current working directory; if non-NULL it should be a valid path (the function will attempt to create it if missing).
filename may be NULL to request an auto-generated random filename; if non-NULL it should be a valid filename (no path traversal or invalid characters for the target filesystem).
truncate must be >= 0 (0 disables truncation).
text must be a valid gboolean value (TRUE to write text for text2pcap, FALSE to write pcap).
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
On success, the returned instance must later be closed via janus_text2pcap_close and freed via janus_text2pcap_free to avoid resource leaks.

functions.name: janus_text2pcap_dump
functions.signature: int janus_text2pcap_dump(janus_text2pcap *instance, janus_text2pcap_packet type, gboolean incoming, char *buf, int len, const char *format, ...); /* G_GNUC_PRINTF(6, 7) */
functions.description: Append a single RTP/RTCP (or data) packet to the active dump file associated with instance. Supports an optional printf-style formatted string (format and varargs) appended to the dump line for extra context. Returns 0 on success, negative on error. Intended to be called for each packet to record, marking whether it was incoming or outgoing.
requirements: instance must be a valid pointer returned by janus_text2pcap_create and not yet freed.
instance must be in a writable state (i.e., successfully created and not closed).
type must be a valid janus_text2pcap_packet enum value.
incoming must be a valid gboolean (TRUE for incoming, FALSE for outgoing).
buf must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer containing the packet bytes to dump.
len must be >= 0; if len > 0, it must not exceed the size of the memory region pointed to by buf.
If instance was created with a nonzero truncate, only up to that many bytes will be written per packet (behavior inferred from the truncate parameter).
If format is non-NULL, it must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with the provided varargs (enforced by G_GNUC_PRINTF(6, 7)); if format is NULL, no extra string is appended.
Caller must check the integer return value and handle negative errors appropriately.
After a failing call due to a non-writable/closed instance, the caller should avoid further dumps until the issue is resolved (inferred).

functions.name: janus_text2pcap_close
functions.description: Close the recorder associated with instance, flushing and closing any underlying file handles. Returns 0 on success, negative on error. After closing, no further packets should be dumped to this instance.
requirements: instance must be a valid pointer returned by janus_text2pcap_create and not yet freed.
Must be called at most once per instance; repeated closes may fail or be no-ops (inferred).
After a successful close, janus_text2pcap_dump must not be called on this instance.
Caller should check and handle the return value; negative values indicate failure.
After closing, release resources with janus_text2pcap_free.

functions.name: janus_text2pcap_free
functions.description: Free a text2pcap recorder instance and its resources. Does not return a value. Typically invoked after janus_text2pcap_close has been called.
requirements: instance may be NULL (behavior unknown; many free-like functions accept NULL, but this is not stated—if unsure, pass a non-NULL pointer).
If the instance still has an open file, the caller should first call janus_text2pcap_close to ensure data integrity and avoid leaks (inferred from API pattern).
After this call, instance must not be used again.

functions.name: janus_plugin_result_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a janus_plugin_result describing the outcome of a plugin request. Used by plugins to return synchronous results (OK with JSON content), asynchronous acknowledgements (OK_WAIT with optional reason text), or core-level errors (ERROR with reason text). Ownership notes: the content JSON reference will be decremented automatically when the result is destroyed; the text pointer is not freed by the result and remains caller-managed.
requirements: type must be one of JANUS_PLUGIN_ERROR, JANUS_PLUGIN_OK, or JANUS_PLUGIN_OK_WAIT.
If type == JANUS_PLUGIN_OK, content must be a valid JSON object/payload; it is ignored otherwise.
If the caller intends to reuse the same content json_t elsewhere, it must json_incref(content) before calling this function, as janus_plugin_result_destroy will json_decref it.
text is only used for JANUS_PLUGIN_OK_WAIT and JANUS_PLUGIN_ERROR; it is ignored for JANUS_PLUGIN_OK.
If text points to dynamically allocated memory, the caller is responsible for freeing it; janus_plugin_result_destroy does not free text.
The returned pointer must be released with janus_plugin_result_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: janus_plugin_result_destroy
functions.description: Destroys and frees a janus_plugin_result previously created with janus_plugin_result_new. This also decrements the reference of the embedded content JSON (if any). It does not free the text pointer.
requirements: result must be a pointer previously returned by janus_plugin_result_new or NULL-safe usage is unknown (not documented).
If result->text was dynamically allocated by the caller, the caller must free it separately before or after calling this function, as this function does not free text.
Do not use the result pointer after destruction.

functions.name: janus_plugin_rtp_extensions_reset
functions.description: Initializes or resets a janus_plugin_rtp_extensions structure to a clean state, setting each supported RTP extension field to its "not present" sentinel (e.g., -1 instead of 0/NULL where applicable). Important when preparing outgoing RTP packets to ensure extensions are interpreted correctly by the core.
requirements: extensions must be a valid, writable pointer to a janus_plugin_rtp_extensions structure.
Call this before populating RTP extension fields for outgoing packets, especially since different extensions use different sentinel values to indicate absence.

functions.name: janus_plugin_rtp_reset
functions.description: Initializes or resets a janus_plugin_rtp packet structure, including its embedded janus_plugin_rtp_extensions. Use before filling in packet fields for send/relay or when reusing a packet struct.
requirements: packet must be a valid, writable pointer to a janus_plugin_rtp structure.
This helper specifically ensures extensions are reset via the embedded janus_plugin_rtp_extensions, so callers that set RTP extensions must call this (or manually reset extensions) before use.

functions.name: janus_plugin_rtp_duplicate
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of a janus_plugin_rtp packet, duplicating both the struct and its RTP buffer. Useful when a plugin needs to retain an incoming packet beyond the caller’s lifetime, since the core passes non-allocated packets to plugins.
requirements: packet must point to a valid janus_plugin_rtp instance provided by the core or previously initialized by the caller.

packet->buffer and packet->length should coherently describe the RTP payload to be duplicated; if buffer is NULL or length is zero the behavior of duplication is implementation-defined (not documented).
The returned packet (if non-NULL) is owned by the caller and must be freed according to the implementation’s expectations (freeing API not documented here).
Function may return NULL on failure; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: janus_plugin_rtcp_reset
functions.description: Initializes or resets a janus_plugin_rtcp packet structure to a clean state before use for send/relay or reuse. Does not specify additional behavior beyond zeroing/clearing fields as appropriate.
requirements: packet must be a valid, writable pointer to a janus_plugin_rtcp structure.

functions.name: janus_plugin_data_reset
functions.description: Initializes or resets a janus_plugin_data message structure to a clean state before sending or when reusing. Applies to text or (future) binary datachannel messages.
requirements: packet must be a valid, writable pointer to a janus_plugin_data structure.
At present only text-based datachannels are supported; binary flag/usage may be ignored by the core until binary support is available (per note).

functions.name: janus_transport_session_create
functions.description: Helper that allocates and initializes a janus_transport_session mapping object used by the Janus core and a transport plugin to associate core-side state with a transport-side session. It stores an opaque transport-side pointer and an optional transport-supplied destructor, and automatically initializes the reference counter.
requirements: transport_p: opaque pointer to the transport-side session instance; the core will not touch this pointer directly (as documented).
p_free: either NULL or a valid function that can free the opaque transport-side session instance; it will be stored and used by the transport/core when appropriate.
The helper automatically initializes the internal reference counter for the mapping instance.
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check the return value before use.

Ownership/lifetime of the returned janus_transport_session is shared; manage references consistently with the rest of the transport’s codebase (details of refcount increments outside this helper are not documented here).

functions.name: janus_transport_session_destroy
functions.description: Helper that marks a janus_transport_session instance as destroyed so the core will no longer use it (e.g., after a WebSocket disconnect or lost HTTP connection). It also adjusts the reference counter corresponding to the create-time reference.
requirements: Call this only when that specific transport session must not be used by the core anymore (per documentation).
If you increased the reference counter elsewhere, you are responsible for decreasing those extra references; this helper only accounts for the reference created by janus_transport_session_create.
The session pointer must refer to a valid janus_transport_session previously created by janus_transport_session_create (inferred from API pairing).

functions.name: janus_transport::init
functions.description: Transport plugin initialization entry point. Called by the Janus core at plugin startup to let the transport set itself up and to provide the janus_transport_callbacks interface and the configuration directory path.
requirements: Must return 0 on success, a negative integer on error (explicit).
callback: non-NULL pointer to core-provided callbacks used by the transport to contact the core (explicit purpose).
config_path: filesystem path to the folder containing this transport’s configuration; the transport may read and parse its config here (explicit purpose).
Should perform one-time setup for the transport (e.g., static initialization and reading config) as part of startup (explicit).

functions.name: janus_transport::destroy
functions.description: Transport plugin deinitialization. Called by the core on shutdown so the transport can clean up its resources.
requirements: Should release all resources allocated by init/startup and stop any running transport activities (implied by destructor purpose).
Must be callable by the core during shutdown; do not block indefinitely.

functions.name: janus_transport::get_api_compatibility
functions.description: Returns the transport plugin API version the plugin was compiled against. The core uses this to verify compatibility.
requirements: Must return JANUS_TRANSPORT_API_VERSION exactly; otherwise the core will reject the plugin (explicit).

functions.name: janus_transport::get_version
functions.description: Returns a numeric version identifier for the transport plugin (e.g., 3). Useful for diagnostics and display.
requirements: Return a non-negative integer representing the plugin version (examples given in docs; exact range not specified).

functions.name: janus_transport::get_version_string
functions.description: Returns a human-readable version string for the transport plugin (e.g., "v1.0.1").
requirements: Return a pointer to a NUL-terminated string with static or otherwise valid lifetime for as long as needed by the caller (common C API practice; exact ownership not stated).

functions.name: janus_transport::get_description
functions.description: Returns a descriptive, human-readable explanation of the transport plugin.
requirements: Return a pointer to a NUL-terminated string; lifetime should remain valid after the call (common C API practice; exact ownership not stated).

functions.name: janus_transport::get_name
functions.description: Returns a short display name for the transport plugin (e.g., "My Amazing Transport").
requirements: Return a pointer to a NUL-terminated string; lifetime should be valid after the call (common C API practice).

functions.name: janus_transport::get_author
functions.description: Returns the author string for the transport plugin.
requirements: Return a pointer to a NUL-terminated string; lifetime should be valid after the call (common C API practice).

functions.name: janus_transport::get_package
functions.description: Returns a unique package identifier for the transport plugin (e.g., "janus.transport.mytransport"). Used by web apps and configuration.
requirements: Return a pointer to a NUL-terminated string that uniquely identifies the plugin package (explicit purpose).
String lifetime should be valid after the call (common C API practice).

functions.name: janus_transport::is_janus_api_enabled
functions.description: Indicates whether the Janus API support is currently enabled in this transport and enabled by the user.
requirements: Return TRUE if Janus API is usable with this transport, FALSE otherwise (explicit).

functions.name: janus_transport::is_admin_api_enabled
functions.description: Indicates whether the Admin API support is currently enabled in this transport and enabled by the user.
requirements: Return TRUE if Admin API is usable with this transport, FALSE otherwise (explicit).

functions.name: janus_transport::send_message
functions.signature: int (* const send_message)(janus_transport_session *transport, void *request_id, gboolean admin, json_t *message);
functions.description: Requests the transport plugin to send a JSON message (response or event) to a client over the specified transport session. A successful return means the message was accepted for sending, not necessarily delivered.
requirements: transport: pointer to the transport session instance to send on (explicit).
request_id: non-NULL only when this is a response correlated to a previous request; may be NULL for events/unsolicited messages (explicit).
admin: set TRUE for Admin API messages, FALSE for Janus API messages (explicit).
message: Jansson json_t object containing the payload (explicit).
The transport plugin is responsible for freeing the message object after handling it (explicit).
Return 0 on success, a negative integer on error (explicit).

functions.name: janus_transport::session_created
functions.description: Notifies the transport plugin that the core created a new Janus session originating from this transport. A transport may react (e.g., by closing the connection) if desired.
requirements: transport: pointer to the related transport session (explicit).
session_id: the newly created session identifier (explicit).

functions.name: janus_transport::session_over
functions.signature: void (* const session_over)(janus_transport_session *transport, guint64 session_id, gboolean timeout, gboolean claimed);
functions.description: Notifies the transport plugin that a session it originated ended, either due to timeout or other reasons. The transport may decide to close the client connection as a result.
requirements: transport: pointer to the related transport session (explicit).
session_id: the session identifier that ended (explicit).
timeout: TRUE if the session closed because of a timeout (explicit).
claimed: TRUE if the session closure was due to someone claiming the session (explicit).

functions.name: janus_transport::session_claimed
functions.description: Notifies the transport plugin that a session it owned was claimed by another transport. The plugin should close the connection as a result.
requirements: transport: pointer to the new transport session instance that has claimed the session (explicit).
session_id: the identifier of the claimed session (explicit).
On receiving this notification, the transport plugin should close the connection (explicit).

functions.name: janus_transport::query_transport
functions.description: Handles a synchronous, transport-specific management request (originating from an Admin API call) and returns a JSON response. Allows tweaking settings or inspecting internals of the transport.
requirements: request: Jansson json_t object containing the management request; structure is handler-specific (explicit).
Must return a Jansson json_t containing the response to be sent back to the Admin API client (explicit).
Request/response formats are transport-specific; there are no constraints imposed by the core (explicit).

functions.name: janus_transport_callbacks::incoming_request
functions.signature: void (* const incoming_request)(janus_transport *plugin, janus_transport_session *transport, void *request_id, gboolean admin, json_t *message, json_error_t *error);
functions.description: Callback for a transport to notify the Janus core of an incoming request from a client. Associates the request with a transport session and provides the JSON payload; may include a transport-specific request identifier and error parsing details.
requirements: plugin: the transport plugin instance originating the request notification (explicit).
transport: pointer to the transport session instance that received the event (explicit).
request_id: opaque transport-specific identifier for correlating later responses (explicit).
